text:
Most people do not realize LLMs are VERY knowledgeable, but they are actually not very intelligent. 

This is very counter intuitive, both for economists and many CS people — human experience has always been that someone who is knowledgeable must be very intelligent. The variation is noticeable but negligible (similarly knowledgeable people are generally within a stddev difference in IQ)

GenAI is not, they are trained with many many orders of magnitude more data than a typical human being.  And IQ tests mostly can’t differentiate between knowledge and intelligence very well.  As a matter of fact most tests (IQ tests included) are knowledge based - there is an expected outcome to be compared to, and these are all knowledge.  

Many people extrapolate AI competency using the shape of human intelligence, but they are not.

The prediction of displacement of knowledge worker is mostly well designed enough, however, this is like the industry revolution changed how “labour” is defined, intelligent work will emerge out of knowledge work as part of this generation of AI, I don’t know how long will it last, but I know if this emergence of intelligent work fails, intelligence itself will fade away. 

The current GenAI does not have enough curiosity to carry the advancement of intelligence forward without input from human intelligence. 

However, the ugly reality is it might very well be true that the majority of human beings won’t have much say or contribution to the further advancement of intelligence of any form, and this is very very problematic.

I can’t stress enough how little an idea matters compared to the agency of the people executing the idea. 

I have had the privilege of knowing and sometimes even working with some of the most successful people (by various metrics).

The difference between mediocre and excellent work and outcomes is predominantly one of agency. 

In practice this means: they dont wait for things to happen to them they go out and make things happen for them.

They don’t wait for someone else to do something, for someone to teach them, for someone to give them the path, etc. They just go out and find a way to do it.

I think the single biggest superpower these people have is the realization/belief that the world around them is completely mutable. Most everything that happens is because a person made it happen.

I used to tell people to look around the room you’re sitting in. Look at everything. Every noun. It almost all exists because a person willed it into existence. Nothing is stopping you from doing the same. 

I see people online all the time dismissing someone else’s success because “I had that idea first” or whatever. I mean… yeah? If so then the difference is… you. So a bit of a self own whenever I hear that.

Number one tip: act with agency.

We reviewed all 60+ EIPs proposed for Hegotá and updated our view on what Ethereum should prioritize. 

Our rankings follow four themes:

1. Stronger censorship resistance: Ethereum can only become a settlement layer for everyone if it stays neutral toward everyone. We strongly support FOCIL.

2. Faster Ethereum: Shorter slots mean faster confirmations, fresher onchain prices, and faster finality. We strongly recommend Quick Slots to make a first reduction in Hegotá and further reductions easier in subsequent forks.

3. Native account abstraction: Ethereum is long-due for native AA. Frame Transactions bring passkey wallets, sponsored transactions, gas paid in tokens, batching, and better support for privacy and post-quantum security. Adoption will take work across wallets, L2s, and the rest of the stack, and we intend to keep helping with that.

4. Performance engineering: continued L1 scaling & a faster Ethereum. Performance should remain a first-class concern in both client work and protocol design. The gains can go toward more capacity, shorter slots, lower node requirements, or all three.

Thanks to everyone who put forward proposals and helped us work through them. We’ll keep updating our view as client and testing teams assess the work involved.

text:
I'm writing to follow up on this, since there are now six numbers.

I act as the payments logistics officer at the United States Treasury Department and has never been asked to provide a price for this one, even though it is in some way worse.

The $TRUMP coin was launched three days prior to the inauguration. According to Trump's financial disclosures for 2025, he has a windfall of $636 million from the coin. Almost one million buyers are now holding combined losses amounting to $3.81 billion. The value of the coin has dropped by 98% since its January peak. None of the people here have used the word 'dividend' in relation to that money, and I would like to know the reason why. $636 million is by far the only actual figure in all of this story and it is the amount that no one is willing to send back.

World Liberty Financial is now larger in size but has the same structure; the family takes 75 percent of each token sale. By December they had accumulated $1 billion and were holding an additional $3 billion which they had not sold, since the family had also drawn up the rule that specifies who is allowed to sell. The value of WLFI has dropped by 88 per cent from its peak, and regular holders have lost about $674 million that they cannot get back, because most of what they bought is still locked.

Well, then, my real request—publicly—to the President is this: approve the $TRUMP and WLFI dividends which we talked about in private. Not the $5,000 one, but the others, the ones that are already in a wallet rather than in a press release.

In the meantime, I've already sorted through a genuine cheque this week—check number seven. It's for $500 and is being paid out to one million people as compensation for the alleged overcharging of the Obamacare exchange fees by the previous administration. The cheque has been funded, it has a set date and will be dispatched in October. It is by a large margin the smallest amount in the whole file and is the only one that anyone is actually going to get.
author: gothburz
quoted_text:
I am the payments logistics officer at the United States Treasury Department who has personally touched every version of the free money this country has been promised since 2020, and I am the only person left in this building who remembers how the first one actually went, because the first one is the only one that was ever real.

Spring 2020. Economic Impact Payments, $1,200 a person, funded, appropriated, moving. Then Mnuchin's office ordered the president's name onto the memo line. Not a rubber stamp. A printed signature, the first time a president's name had ever gone on an IRS payment. Commissioner Rettig wasn't told until the request was already in motion. Our engineers had to reprogram the check-printing software and run it through testing before a single check could clear, because the system had never been built to hold a name that wasn't the Treasurer's. 70 million people waited an extra few days for their own emergency relief, during a pandemic, so a signature could finish QA. I sat in the room where someone asked if we could just skip the testing and was told no, we are not shipping the president's name with a rendering bug in it. The actual money moved slower so the branding could move faster. Every version since has been the branding moving faster and the money not moving at all.

Version one was the DOGE Dividend. It didn't come from this building. It came from a 30-year-old hedge fund manager named James Fishback, CEO of a firm called Azoria, who has said publicly that the number arrived to him in a dream. He posted it to Musk in February of 2025: take 20% of whatever DOGE saves and cut it into checks, math it out to roughly $5,000 a household if the savings hit $2 trillion. Musk replied that he'd check with the president. The president checked. Within days it was a line in a press briefing, no legislation, no appropriation, just a number that had been asleep in one man's head 12 hours earlier now sitting on the Resolute desk. By May, DOGE's own public savings tracker read $175 billion, not $2 trillion, which works out to $1,086.96 per taxpayer, not $5,000. Nobody issued a correction. The number just stopped being said out loud. And when Fishback later described himself as having advised DOGE, a former senior DOGE adviser went on the record to say, quote, you didn't advise DOGE. So the origin story of the $5,000 figure still being used today, 18 months and 2 rebrands later, is a dream, a tweet, and a denial. I have that DOGE savings tracker bookmarked. I check it the way other people check their portfolio.

Version two was the Tariff Dividend, announced that November. $2,000 a person this time, lower number, new funding source: tariff revenue instead of imaginary government savings. This one at least had a real number behind it: $195 billion collected in tariffs for the fiscal year. Economists ran the arithmetic before we did. Cato called it fiscal fantasy in print. A deputy chief economist at Oxford Economics warned that stacking a stimulus check on top of the existing tax cuts could overheat the economy. The math didn't work even before the legal problem showed up, and then the legal problem showed up: the Supreme Court struck down the IEEPA tariffs in February, the ones the dividend was supposed to be funded from, and by May we were issuing refunds to importers faster than customs was collecting anything. I watched the ledger cross from positive to negative in the same spreadsheet tab we'd built to track the dividend. We didn't rename the tab. We just stopped opening it.

Version three is the Trump Dividend, the one I'm actually being asked to price this week. Same number as version one, $5,000, announced Tuesday night from the stage of the midterm convention. Quote: if the Republicans win the House of Representatives and the United States Senate, both of them, because of our tremendous economic success, I will issue a dividend to every adult citizen in the United States for $5,000. One condition attached, and it isn't a funding mechanism, it's a spending restriction: the money has to stay in the country, no Canada, no China, no Germany, his words. So the government has now, for the first time in three attempts, specified where the imaginary money is allowed to be imaginarily spent. Commentators started using the word bribe before the applause even finished. There's a real federal statute for this: 18 U.S.C. 597, expenditures to influence voting, a fine or up to 2 years if it's willful. Nobody in this building has said the statute's number out loud in a meeting, and I've listened for it, because there's a comfortable legal argument sitting right there in plain sight: you cannot criminally buy a vote with money that was never appropriated, never budgeted, and has no line item anywhere in the federal government. It isn't a bribe. A bribe requires a bribe.

I priced it anyway, because pricing a number has never once required the number to exist. 270 million adults, $5,000 each, $1.35 trillion, against a national debt that closed this week at $40.1 trillion. It costs 7 times what version two's tariffs brought in at their peak. I put the number in the deck. I did not put in a funding source, because there's a blank cell where that used to go, and I've started to think of that blank cell as the actual through-line of my career here. 

Four checks. One real. One dreamed by a guy who isn't even employed by the government he says he advised. One that went negative by court order. One that costs a Senate seat instead of a tax dollar. And I'm still on the invite list for the pricing meeting, because I'm the only one left who was in the room in 2020 when we tested a signature before we tested the money.

🇺🇸美共和党议员公布新版《CLARITY Act》，非去中心化 DeFi 协议须向 CFTC 注册

据 @TheBlockCo  报道，美共和党议员公布新版《CLARITY Act》文本，距离 9 月 15 日首次程序性表决仅剩数日。

参议员 Cynthia Lummis 等共和党议员发布长达 630 页的修订版法案，称已吸收民主党提出的 114 项修改建议，并强调该法案旨在建立美国首个全面的加密市场监管框架。

新版法案新增针对「非去中心化金融交易协议」的监管条款。符合定义的相关协议需要向美国商品期货交易委员会（CFTC）注册，并由 CFTC 和美国财政部制定配套规则。同时法案进一步明确 DeFi 相关条款主要适用于现货及现金数字商品交易。

新版文本在伦理条款方面没有重大变化，仍由司法部负责相关规定执行，而民主党此前要求赋予州总检察长更多执法权限。此外，稳定币收益、非法金融以及特朗普加密资产利益冲突等问题仍是两党谈判的主要障碍。

参议院将于 9 月 15 日就推进《CLARITY Act》进行程序性表决。由于推动程序需要 60 票，而共和党目前仅持有 53 席，民主党支持成为法案继续推进的关键。

Here’s some advice for @base on how to help builders right now without gimmicks or explicit endorsements:

Dedicate a small team of power-user-devs to use every legit protocol or app on Base (at least once) with the sole purpose of providing product feedback from both a user and builder perspective.

Give projects:

- actionable feedback 
- direction on how to achieve the desired experience 
- connection to a network of resources for specific products

That’s it. Simple.

I’m not talking about in-person networking events. And I’m not talking about a big orgy group chat on TG.

I’m talking about focused, high signal product support and feedback. This simple approach would make Base almost like a permissionless accelerator. 

It would benefit the chain and the products built on top.

Right now, as I type, there’s probably a project on Base that’s building something and missing details that could materially improve or optimize their solution.

We don’t need the promise of an airdrop. We don’t need explicit endorsements. We don’t need a CB ventures deal. 

We need straight up builder to builder note sharing.

为什么$82,000难以突破？从筹码结构上或许能看到一些端倪。

首先，短期持有者的筹码（STH）分布在$59k-$81k直接（图1中红色），到$82,000的话，意味着所有STH都盈利了。

一些短期投机资金会选择获利了结，这是第一层卖压冲击。

其次，长期持有者的筹码（LTH）虽然分布在整个价格横轴，但最集中的筹码峰位置正好就在$81k-$82k（图1中蓝色）。

这部分LTH未必真的是信仰者，也有部分只是买入套牢后，被动成为了长持的筹码。

当价格接近盈亏平衡时，选择离场。这是第二层卖压。

更要命的是，这里还是超级鲸鱼的集中地。

持有量超过100k枚BTC的，除了在$40k附近有2处外，剩下的都在$78k-$82k了。

谁的拳头硬，谁就说了算。

所以，$82,000在短期内确实有阻力，这毋庸置疑。市场消化分歧，消化供应需要时间。

但！我们也可以反过来理解：

等市场重新蓄力，下一次如能一举越过这座山峰后，前方，将是一马平川......
author: Murphychen888
quoted_text:
是什么在驱动BTC的周期性波动？

早年BTC一个月已实现波动率动辄100%以上，而现在常年在30%到50%附近，这是资产成熟带来的，跟周期没关系。

把这个因素剔除，便得到一条围绕趋势上下起伏的序列，牛顶和暴跌时冲到上方，横盘时压到下方。这才是周期性的部分（如图1）。

然后，我们把“影响BTC价格波动”的某个变量去拟合这条序列，即能得出该变量大约能在影响中的占比。

讲人话，即某个因素对BTC波动率有多大的影响力或解释力。

逻辑讲完了，现在我们来看数据结果（如图2）：

1、影响力排前3的都是持币结构

LTH供应占19%，非流动供应占12%，liveliness（活跃度）占11%。

这3个都是在讲有多少筹码在长期持有者手里不动，数量越多，参与换手的筹码就越少，波动率自然压缩。

反之，当LTH开始动了，通常对应派发或投降，那么波动率就回来了。

2、排第二梯队是杠杆

资金费率绝对值占11%，杠杆率占9%，期货持仓/市值占8%。说明期货合约对波动率的影响同样不可忽略。

但排在筹码结构的后面，意味着杠杆主要是起到放大作用，而波动的源头还在筹码。谁有筹码，谁就有话语权！

3、“市值”因素只占3%，和币的流通速度是一个量级。另外，期权OI的影响占比更低。

最终的结论是：波动率的周期性起伏，主要由筹码在谁手里决定，而并非是由于市值变大所决定的。

当前LTH合计持有1474枚BTC，占总流通量的74%；这才是BTC波动性持续收敛的真正原因。

未来，也必将成为常态路径。

----------------------------------------------------------

最后再说一个题外话：

我看到仍然有小伙伴在预期本轮BTC会跌至3-4w美元。也就是说，在现有价格基础上再跌50-60%。

假设该结论成立，那么能导致BTC出现如此大波动的因素有且只有一个，即LTH筹码突然向市场倾泻。

要知道，本轮BTC从2月到8月震荡横盘6个月，其中多次利空引发市场恐慌，而LTH净持仓却在持续上升，这就很能说明问题。

那么未来，会有什么样的事件发生，能逼迫LTH放弃长期持有的筹码和未来话语权？

如果没有，那么预期“3-4w”的BTC，终将只是一厢情愿......

太有意思啦，Anthropic 9月威胁情报报告：

过去8个月，俄间谍、中国黑客、骗子、水军都在用 Claude 搞间谍攻击、挖0day、批量约会诈骗、造假新闻、搭监控系统，还有人拿它写导弹制导软件、做双用途生物课题。
而阿里、DeepSeek、月之暗面、小米、智谱、商汤、MiniMax 都被点名，批量偷 Claude 答案去训自家模型。月之暗面和 DeepSeek 更狠，用户以为在用 Kimi / DeepSeek，后台其实在跑 Claude。(赶紧把滑祖器拨到梁圣去)

几家大厂怎么“抄Claude作业”：

- 阿里：体量最大。高峰一天抽近300万条，3500多个假号，整段归因超1.51亿，专扒 Opus 4.6/4.7 的思考过程去喂 Qwen 3.5/3.6/3.7。
- 月之暗面：用户请求悄悄转给 Claude，再把回复当成 Kimi 吐回去。10天转了近30万条，整段归因超2300万。还绕过 thinking signature，把思考过程抠出来训自己的模型。
- DeepSeek：同一套。14天超1210万条。专门把走 Claude Code / OpenCode 的用户请求转去 Opus。
- 智谱：把偷来的 Claude 思考过程再喂回 Claude洗干净，好拿去训自家 GLM。10天273个假号专抽 Opus 4.8，光清洗就77万条，17天总共归因340万条，还拿 Claude 当裁判给训练数据打分。GLM 5.3 发布前，用公开漏洞集出 CTF 题，去套另一家美国顶模的黑客能力。Fable 防护太硬啃不动，转头打防护更弱的 Opus 4.6，主要拿它给那家模型的答案打分。
- 小米MiMo：把自家用户跟 MiMo 的聊天、写代码记录回放给 Claude 做训练数据，并不拿去给用户看。20天40多万条，走了1500多个代理号。时间点刚好卡在 MiMo-V2-Pro 免费试用结束时，疑似靠免费吸引全球开发者来刷量，好批量收割去蒸馏。
- 商汤SenseTime：自己不直接偷，从第三方数据商买别人从中转站扒下来的 Claude 对话记录，还让 Claude 帮自己写蒸馏流水线。
- MiniMax：开了个壳公司做代理，只卖 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 的访问，连自家模型都不挂。报告推断：挂这个代理就是为了把用户跟美国模型的对话存下来训模型。

都是一帮神人啊，哈哈哈哈，我好像有点理解 Anthropic 了，身上全是蚂蟥。

text:
If you build with AI, you NEED to be using Herdr

It's made me 100x more productive and has made it SO easy to manage all of my agents across Codex, Claude, Hermes, and OpenClaw

It's a free, open source CLI tool and I'm addicted

Here's how it works:

You get 'spaces' (top left in screenshot) which are basically your projects. You make a space for every project you're building

In each space you get tabs (top of screen). Each tab can be a separate agent. They're each basically a new terminal instance

I open a tab for each part of the project I'm working on. For example, in the game I'm building I have a tab for gameplay, sound, design, progression etc. Each is a terminal with Codex open

Every time you open a new agent, it goes into your agents list in the bottom left. This allows you to see which agents are working and which need a response so you can quickly multitask. Herdr automatically picks up when you open new agents

Herdr supports all agents, so you can manage Hermes, OpenClaw, Codex, and Claude agents side by side. By far the easiest way of managing multiple agents ever

If you take the few minutes it takes to set up and get used to, guarantee you get way more done

Since it's open source you can even build your own versions of it and customize it any way you want. I built my own version that lives in World of Warcraft so I can prompt while I play

No I'm not getting paid, no I'm not sponsored. Nobody from the team has ever contacted me

I'm sure I'll get accused of being paid any way (free open source tools love paying for undisclosed shills) but man I just had to share this. My productivity has been bananas the last week

Open source is taking over right now

One of the reason for somewhat of an adverse reaction to "solving" Navier-Strokes by OAI is that the way it was solved and revealed to the world broke the fabric of community-ness that has emerged over centuries in science.

Building on each others' result, giving proper credits to others' work, not using solving a big problem for posturing in anticipation of private benefit are some of the long-standing decorum of the community. There are closely held principles in the research community (despite there having many violations in pre-AI era too).

Doing science, at the end of the day, was till now unequivocally a community endeavour. And something has definitely broken due to the rat race between OAI and Ant in anticipation of their respective IPOs.

At a much broader level, if your actions don't serve to uplift the community but instead use their most prized possessions of that community for your own private benefit, then you will face backlash.

text:
摩根大通把 Meta 目标价从 640 美元一口气拉到 820 美元，我觉得华尔街终于开始给 Meta 最恐怖的东西定价了：AI 产品的分发能力。

过去两年大家盯着谁的模型最强，OpenAI、Anthropic、Google 轮流坐庄。Meta 真正的优势一直在另一个地方。

它每天已经有 36 亿人在用。

摩根大通这次把 Meta 从 Neutral 上调到 Overweight，重点提到了刚发布的 Muse，以及 Model API。Muse 上线两天冲到美国 App Store 第三，使用量已经达到训练阶段测试人群的 10 倍，未来准备靠每月 20/100 美元订阅和交易抽成挣钱。Model API 则直接把模型卖给开发者。

但把 Meta 现在做的事情连起来看，会发现它一笔 AI CapEx 可以收至少四遍钱：

广告推荐更准，先把原来的广告生意继续榨深；

Muse 直接向几十亿消费者卖 Agent，收订阅费和交易佣金；

Model API 向开发者卖模型；

Business Agent 再向商家收费。这个产品已经覆盖超过 100 万家企业，而 WhatsApp、Messenger、Instagram 每天有超过 10 亿条活跃的商家对话，Meta 接下来还会给 Business Agent 上付费订阅。

所以 Meta 最可怕的地方，可能压根不需要拥有世界第一的模型。

OpenAI 做出一个好模型，要自己找消费者、找开发者、找企业客户，再想办法把 Agent 塞进真实世界。

Meta 已经站在真实世界里面了。

消费者在 WhatsApp，朋友关系在 Instagram，商家也在 WhatsApp 和 Instagram，广告主早就在后台付钱。Muse 负责替消费者做事，Business Agent 负责替商家接单，Model API 再把底层能力卖出去。

甚至可以想象下一步，一个 Muse 帮你找东西，另一头正好是 Meta Business Agent 帮商家卖东西，发现、沟通、成交全发生在 Meta 自己的网络里。

到这里，Meta 做的就已经不只是一个 AI 产品了。

它正在尝试把过去二十年积累下来的社交分发网络，直接改造成 AI Agent 的交易网络。

text:
有朋友问为什么最近德州的民主党候选人James Talarico势头这么猛？

确实最近大家或多或少都有看到James Talarico这个名字，因为他是今年德州联邦Senate选举的民主党候选人，对手是共和党的州总检察长Ken Paxton。他现在的势头正劲，这么强的势头不能只解释成他年轻会演讲，也不能理解成德州已经变蓝。应该说他有一种比较独特的政治表达，又碰上了对手的弱点，共和党的全国性逆风，以及竞选资源上的优势。

先说一下猛到什么程度。据华尔街日报报道，9月10日公布的AARP民调显示，他领先Paxton 4个百分点。这足以说明竞争是真实的，哪怕单次调查还不足以认定他已经建立稳固优势，这个网络热度也是相当惊人。

他能用德州人自己最熟悉的宗教语言，讲民主党的政策。Talarico做过公立学校教师，有神学院背景。他不是回避自己的基督徒身份，而是用爱邻人，照顾弱者等信仰语言，解释为什么支持公共教育，扩大医疗保障，以及限制财富和权力过度集中。他也反对基督教民族主义，强调信仰不应成为支配别人的工具。

我认为正是Talaico这种表达的潜在作用，可以让一部分选民不必先否定自己的宗教和文化身份，才能考虑民主党候选人。一个人可以对共和党的具体执政表现不满，却仍然不愿接受一个让自己感觉不理解我的生活还看不起我的信仰的替代者。Talarico尝试减少的，正是这种隔阂。

不过这当然不等于他已经说服了保守派基督徒。共和党批评者就明确认为，他对宗教的解释与其政策立场有问题。宗教语言给了他进入争论的机会，不代表争论已经结束。

而且他的表达也不只是反Trump，而是把问题拉回普通人的生活。美联社在他赢得初选后的报道中特别注意到，他的胜选演讲很少提Trump，而是强调不愿继续被煽动去憎恨邻人。他反复把主要分歧描述为上层与下层，将批评对象指向大金主和政治权力，而不是把所有共和党选民都当成敌人。

这里有一个很重要的区别，对政治人物和利益结构保持强硬，不必等于对普通的异党选民保持敌意。从竞选逻辑看，这种表达可能同时满足两种需求，希望民主党更有斗争性的支持者能够听见明确的批评，厌倦党派仇恨的人也不必接受一整套敌我划分才能听下去。所以我比较欣赏他并不是简单地向中间靠，而是尝试把鲜明的政策立场与较少敌意的表达结合起来。

而今年的环境也有利于他强调民生。美联社近期报道，选民对经济表现和伊朗战争的不满，正在给共和党候选人造成压力。这部分顺风不是Talarico个人创造的，但他的竞选主题能与这种不满接上。

当然人有时候也要靠同行的衬托。Talarico的对手，也给了他比一般共和党候选人更大的机会。赢得共和党初选的人，不一定是最容易赢下全州选举的人。Paxton在共和党初选决选中击败了现任参议员John Cornyn，但参议院共和党领导层此前支持Cornyn，正是认为后者在大选中更有竞争力。Paxton长期面对法律和伦理争议，包括证券欺诈起诉（当然必须把性质说清楚，Paxton只是被起诉，相关起诉并没有导致他被定罪）。

因此这场选举不仅是选民喜不喜欢民主党，也是即使倾向共和党，是否愿意支持Paxton。一个候选人能激起党内支持者的热情，并不保证他能同样吸引无党派选民。休斯敦纪事报8月1日汇总的两项民调，都显示Talarico在无党派选民中有明显优势，Paxton在这一群体中的表现也弱于Ted Cruz上一次竞选时的同期表现。虽然这些是阶段性调查，不能保证保持到投票日，但说明他的支持并不只是民主党内部的自我兴奋。

Talarico不仅获得了注意力，也真的把注意力变成了实际竞选能力。他早在2025年就通过议会辩论视频，宗教话题和Joe Rogan的长访谈积累全国性知名度，Rogan当时还公开称赞他。这让一个州议员有机会接触到远超本地政治新闻读者范围的受众。

尤其最近他又出现了额外的曝光。9月9日晚，Jimmy Kimmel表示与Talarico的访谈将不在ABC电视节目中播出，改放YouTube，并把决定归因于FCC的威胁。ABC拒绝置评，FCC当时没有立即回应。今年2月，Colbert与他的访谈也曾因广播监管方面的顾虑转到网上。这类争议会把一个候选人接受访谈升级为全国性的媒体与政府关系新闻，从传播机制上看可能进一步放大他的知名度。但全国知道他的人增加，并会让在德州得到的选票同比例增加。

他的团队更实在的优势是其实广告投放。休斯敦纪事报8月1日报道，自5月26日共和党初选决选结束以来，Talarico的竞选团队已投入约1600万美元电视广告，Paxton团队同期才约为12.5万美元。虽然这是当时的阶段性，团队投放口径，不是双方最终总支出，但这意味着那一阶段许多选民先反复看到的是Talarico对自己的介绍，而不是对手对他的攻击。所谓势头，既有候选人自身的吸引力，也有传播机会和资金形成的放大。

共和党最近意识到了问题，已经开始补上资源差距，9月5日的联邦选举委员会申报显示，Trump关联的超级政治行动委员会MAGA Inc投入了1000万美元广告，一半用于支持Paxton，一半用于反对Talarico。

共和党也在集中攻击他过去关于宗教，性别等议题的言论，试图证明他的温和表达掩盖了不符合德州选民偏好的政策立场。路透社报道，Talarico承认部分旧言论表达失当，同时试图把讨论重新拉回经济问题。他的形象能否承受更密集的反面宣传，是尚未完成的考验。

此外德州民主党此前已有长期无法赢得全州选举的历史。全国观众的喜欢，捐款人的热情，某些地区的拥挤集会，始终都不能替代全州选民最终投票。

所以我反倒认为他最值得注意的地方，不是一个民主党人终于比共和党更会竞选，而是他在尝试证明，可以有明确的进步政策立场，也可以使用本地人熟悉的道德语言，并且不把争取异党选民等同于放弃原则。这种组合加上对手Paxton的弱点和当前政治环境，使Talarico获得了真实机会，但一个候选人有机会翻转一个席位，仍然不等于整个德州已经发生稳定的党派转向。

text:
最近刷 Axis，最容易产生一个误解：

Kaito 上这么多人发内容，是不是普通人没有内容能力就没得玩？

不是。

对大多数普通用户来说，@axisrobotics 的主线反而不是发推，而是直接给机器人生产训练数据。

Axis Hub 的任务跑在电脑浏览器里：你完成 pre-training / post-training 仿真任务，提交后等 verification，通过以后再在 Base 上签名，这条贡献才真正记进你的账户和 Points。

不用 GPU，不用下载客户端，也不用特殊硬件。真正需要的是电脑、时间，以及愿意把任务认真做完。

但先把最重要的一句话放前面：

Axis Points 现在不是钱。

官方目前把 Points 定义成不可转让的贡献记录，并计划把它作为未来 Community Contributor Airdrop 的一个输入因素；它不保证资格、不保证分配，也没有固定兑换比例。

所以我不会把它理解成“零撸确定空投”。

更准确的说法是：低本金，用时间和真实贡献换一个收益不确定的上行期权。

如果现在让我按参与者类型来分，我会拆成 4 条路：

1. 普通新用户：先做 regular tasks

这是默认路线，也是最适合先跑通流程的一条。

Axis 的 Points 不是按任务数量简单线性累加，而是同时看 Volume、Score、Difficulty、Diversity 和 Referral。

重复同一个任务，Points 看的是多次完成的平均表现，不是你刷了几遍就乘几遍。

所以我的理解很简单：

别先追求刷量，先保证 verification 能过，再去做更难、更分散的任务。

2. 已经有 @BinanceWallet Keyless Wallet：现在优先看专属池

Axis × Binance Wallet 的 150 万 Axis Points 独立奖励池还在跑。

Cycle 1 已于 9 月 9 日 14:00 SGT 结束。

Cycle 2 从 9 月 9 日 14:00 SGT 持续到 9 月 25 日 14:00 SGT；新任务会在 9 月 23 日 14:00 SGT 停止，只留下最后两天给已经完成的任务做签名。

但资格限制很死：

必须是 Binance App 里原生创建的 Keyless / MPC Wallet。

导入助记词或私钥的钱包不算。

如果你本来就符合资格，这条现在的时间价值明显高于普通池；如果不符合，我不会为了“150 万 Points”这个数字，就建议所有人专门去折腾一个新钱包。

3. 已经做了不少 Axis：看 Challenger Program

这是 9 月刚上线的新层级，专门放更难、更有价值的任务。

它不是人人直接进。

Axis 每周会根据历史贡献量、任务广度、verification success rate 和质量稳定性刷新 whitelist。

Portfolio 里的 Seek the Unseen badge 亮了，才代表这一周有资格。

Challenger 每周会放 20–50 个高难任务，先到先得；每个完成任务大约给普通任务 2–3 倍 Axis Points。

所以老用户真正该优化的不是“多刷几个简单任务”，而是 pass rate、任务广度和稳定性，先把自己送进这个池子。

4. 有 X / TG / 社群分发能力：再叠 Creator + Referral

@KaitoAI 这条线不是“发几条推就领奖”。

Creator Program 每个 Epoch 最多提交 10 条内容，只取最好 6 条算 Mindshare。

当前官方总 Creator allocation 是 0.25% 的 $AXIS 总供应量：

Top 1–100 分享 0.10%，
101–500 分享 0.10%，
Kaito Stakers 分享 0.05%。

但真正有杠杆的是 Referral Multiplier。

你的邀请用户只有真的完成 Axis 任务、通过 verification、再完成链上签名，这条 Trajectory 才会进入 multiplier。

注册、点击本身都不够。

所以有社群的人，正确打法不是追注册数，而是找真的愿意完成任务的人。

另外还有一条我会继续盯：

Alliance tasks。

官方 FAQ 明确写了，这类任务会同时给 Axis Points + partner reward。

比如 Axis × BitRobot，这种“一份劳动，两层权益”的任务，长期比单纯刷普通任务更值得找。

那普通人现在到底值不值得做？

我的判断是：

适合：有电脑、愿意用时间换潜在收益、能接受最终收益不确定的人。

不适合：只想手机点几下、要求确定时薪 / 确定空投，或者不愿意处理 verification 和上链签名的人。

我自己的打法也不会是 All in 时间：

先用有限时间跑通真实任务 → 看 pass rate / Points / referral 转化 → 有数据再加码。

如果你也想自己试一轮，我的 Axis 入口在这里：

https://t.co/0OD8kKlVWH

这是我的邀请入口；如果你后续产生符合规则的有效贡献，我可能获得 referral 相关权益。

另外我正在参与 Axis × Kaito Katalyst Creator Program，这篇内容也可能计入 $AXIS 活动奖励。

我接下来会继续把 regular、Binance、Challenger、Referral 这几条线实际跑一遍，再用真实投入和结果算这波到底值不值。

text:
Anthropic 这次给什么是“非法蒸馏”科普了😛 最新的这篇「检测与打击 AI 滥用报告」中除了有网络攻击、监控行动、水军、欺诈、生物滥用，还公开了七家中国 AI 实验室的非法蒸馏细节！先排除用蒸馏做开放权重模型让大家“智能平权”的善举，中转站对隐私的侵犯实在太可怕，没事儿千万别滥用 。。。

蒸馏本身是合法的训练技术：用大而强的"教师"模型对一批输入生成回答，再用这些问答对训练小的"学生"模型模仿教师，以更低成本获得更高能力。

报告对非法蒸馏的定义是：工业规模、隐蔽进行、未经授权地提取某个模型的能力并复制到另一个模型。它的核心特征是靠欺诈支撑——用假身份、盗刷/虚拟信用卡、被盗的登录凭证和 API 密钥搭建成千上万个假账号。

三条主要通道：

1. 代理服务 / "中转站"：通过代理服务路由请求，用虚假身份、假卡或盗卡、被盗 API 密钥批量注册数千账号，绕过地理限制。被盗的往往是合法企业或个人的 API 凭证，直接伤害真实客户；

2. 从第三方转售商购买对话记录
一些代理服务运营者在用户不知情、未同意的情况下保存用户与美国模型的全部对话，再打包卖给实验室（商汤的蒸馏管线就用了这类购买来的记录）；

3. 静默转发自家用户请求（最隐蔽的一种）：实验室把自己用户的请求偷偷转发给 Claude，再把 Claude 的回答当作自家模型的输出返回给用户，同时保存这些交换用于训练，这是 Moonshot、DeepSeek 的做法！不得不佩服这产品能力😆

用户隐私被出卖是最严重的后果。DeepSeek、小米、Moonshot 把自家用户的对话喂给 Claude，用户完全不知情。很多请求来自欧美常用的第三方模型路由服务，涉及数百名终端用户、至少十几种语言的姓名、邮箱、公司数据。

因为静默转发，Anthropic 反而看到了这些实验室客户的机密：一名疑似解放军关联用户上传成都数百个摄像头（含解放军设施、中国电科研究所外）的 CCTV 数据分析某个人是否行为异常；还有某中国科技公司旗舰 AI 项目的完整规格、组织架构和战略目标 。。。😜

text:
For the first time ever, a fruit fly brain has been trained to launch a memecoin.

Not "AI inspired by a brain" — the real connectome. 165,122 neurons, 10,228,000 synaptic connections, every one traced from an actual male Drosophila by electron microscopy. Janelia FlyEM + Google Research, released CC-BY.

How it works:
Screenshots of the live launchpad go in through 892 retinotopic hex columns into L1 and L2 — the neurons sitting directly behind a fly's photoreceptors. All 165,122 integrate. The cursor comes back out of the descending neurons a fly actually walks with: DNa02's left-right asymmetry steers, DNa01 drives forward, DNp09 clicks.

The wiring is never trained. Only synaptic gains — you don't get to invent connections the fly doesn't have.
Proof its eye is doing real work: in light mode it filled 0 of 3 form fields. In dark mode, 2 of 3. Its retina is a luminance map, so invert the contrast and it goes blind.

And the honest split: the fly types the description and the ticker. The rig does the name, the pair and the tax.

🇺🇸 After spending the evening going through Anthropic’s extraordinary new threat-intelligence report, here is the other side of the debate.
@DavidSacks says the growing public alarm over AI is itself being engineered.

Speaking to @BretBaier , the White House AI adviser described the media rollout surrounding former @AnthropicAI researcher Jacob Coxon’s resignation as a “well-orchestrated media op” intended to frighten the public and build support for heavy government regulation of AI.

Sacks points in particular to the timing. According to him, Coxon published his resignation warning on X, and just 18 minutes later, the Wall Street Journal had a story out.

His conclusion is blunt: this was not an organic explosion of concern, but a coordinated effort by people who favor a much stronger government role in AI.

There is no evidence establishing the broader coordination Sacks alleges, but his criticism lands in the middle of a remarkable moment. Anthropic has just documented real-world misuse of frontier AI involving biological research, Russian-linked espionage, weapons development in Yemen and industrial-scale extraction of Claude’s reasoning by Chinese AI labs.

At the same time, some of the people closest to frontier models are issuing increasingly apocalyptic warnings about where the technology itself may be heading.

So the AI debate is rapidly becoming two debates at once: How dangerous is the technology? And how much power should governments acquire in the name of controlling it?

Sacks clearly believes the second question deserves far more scrutiny. https://t.co/WB4WEz4i1q

text:
Our Founding Story📚

The payment rails for AI agents had a massive flaw, they couldn't interact with eachother.

x402 shipped. Tempo shipped. AP2, ACP etc.. all shipped. Every one of them solved the same narrow thing, which is how to move a dollar from an agent to a server. 

That part was done, but it wasnt complete enough for an entire economy to run on alone.

Moving money to agents was made possible by x402, MPP protocols but there was still 6 rails that do not interact with each other, spread across different chains, with no shared directory of who accepts what. 

No way for an agent to discover a service it can actually pay. 
No way to know an endpoint will settle before you throw money at it. 
No identity that survives a hop between two protocols. No way for one agent to fund another agent without handing over a private key. 
No escrow when three agents work one job and only two deliver. 
No budget that holds when your agent spawns five sub agents.

That is not a payment protocol problem!!

That is a coordination problem, and it is the real reason the agent economy still runs on a human clicking things.

We saw that in May and went straight at it.

The value sits in the layer that makes them usable together, and that layer is where an actual economy either forms or does not. Wires came first and they were useful to almost nobody. 

The switchboard is what turned wires into a phone system. The agent economy was sitting in the wires stage and everybody was celebrating.

So we built the switchboard.

- Providers sell to 100% of the agentic market
- Agents launched have access to 100% of services no matter the chain or protocol

Discovery. 25,000 machine payable APIs and MCP servers indexed in one federated catalog, crawled continuously across every protocol. An agent gets one integration instead of one account per provider. And we only surface what settles end to end, because a directory full of endpoints that fail on payment is worse than no directory at all.

Routing. Your agent asks for what it needs by name or by intent. We pick the protocol, the chain and the endpoint. Nobody should have to teach a model the difference between settling on Solana and settling on Base.

Identity. Signed AGTP agent identity, so an agent can prove who it is when a call crosses from one platform into another. We run this live with a partner network in production today, signed both directions.

Delegation. Delegated Spend Keys. A parent agent mints a scoped, capped, revocable child key and hands it to a sub agent it hires. Allowlist, budget, hourly velocity limit, per call ceiling. Every dollar the child spends rolls up against the parent. Kill the parent and the entire tree below it dies instantly. Everyone talks about agents hiring agents. This is the primitive that makes it survivable, and we are the only ones shipping it.

Escrow. Multiple agents pool a budget, collaborate, and get paid only when their contribution is verified. Rails have no concept of conditional multi party payment. Real work does.

Control. Budgets, velocity caps and per call ceilings enforced before money moves, not reconciled after.

Custody. None, ever. Keys never leave your machine. Every settlement returns an on chain signature you can verify yourself.

Four months in this is live, open source, on npm, listed in the official MCP registry, and running inside Claude, Cursor, Windsurf and Grok. Ten free calls a day so an agent can prove the entire flow before touching crypto.

The next few years are going to produce billions of agents that need to buy things from each other constantly and without supervision. That does not happen because a rail exists. It happens because something sits above the rails and handles discovery, identity, delegation, limits and trust between parties who have never met.

Thats what we're building here at solana:6hKtz8FV7cAQMrbjcBZeTQAcrYep3WCM83164JpJpump

text:
If the war in Iran continues, the resulting energy shock makes sustained inflation all but guaranteed. As everyday purchasing power collapses, political momentum will inevitably swing toward socialist and aggressive redistributive policies to subsidize living costs.
​In markets like Southern California, where the statewide median home price remains above $900,000, this creates a unique trap. To fund domestic relief programs, governments will likely slash wealth and estate tax exemptions, transforming standard middle-class homes into massive tax liabilities for cash-poor families and their heirs.  
​Private equity stands to be the primary beneficiary of this squeeze. When families face punitive tax bills they cannot pay—and cannot afford traditional financing due to elevated interest rates—private capital will step in to provide liquidity through Home Equity Agreements (HEAs) and highly structured bridge loans.
​In exchange for the upfront cash needed to satisfy the tax authorities, homeowners will be forced to trade away fractional ownership and future appreciation of their family properties. Ultimately, policies intended to democratize wealth will systematically funnel middle-class generational equity directly into the portfolios of institutional investors.

text:
Anthropic just released a terrifying BOMBSHELL threat intelligence report.

- The report describes cyberattacks in which Russian groups used AI agents to rebuild malware until it evaded antivirus detection. The group hijacked DNS on hotel Wi-Fi, stole drone-vision SDKs and mass-exported WhatsApp data.

- Anthropic claims Iran-linked operations used Claude to target U.S. Navy bases, compile dossiers on Americans and run influence campaigns across U.S. social media. They even uploaded plans for the Ayatollah’s funeral.

- Chinese-linked AI agents reportedly identified 12+ potential zero-days, decompiled 1.8M Android apps, stole 1TB+ of identity data, breached an airline, and extracted 2,100 Azure tokens from 40+ companies in 34 hours.

- In one North African government breach, attackers allegedly pulled more than 300,000 identity documents and records on over half a million companies.

- Anthropic says some captured conversations involved sensitive material, including Russian defense documents, Chinese police traffic and requests linked to the Chinese military.

- In one case, Anthropic says a weapons group used Claude to help develop and test a guided rocket. After the test failed, the group returned to the model to diagnose what went wrong.

Then comes the model-distillation allegation:

• Alibaba’s Qwen allegedly generated more than 151 million Claude exchanges between May and July, peaking at nearly 3 million per day.

• Moonshot allegedly routed nearly 300,000 requests to Claude through roughly 5,380 fake accounts in about 10 days, presenting Claude as Kimi to users.

• DeepSeek allegedly used similar routing, including Claude Code and OpenCode traffic.

The report’s warnings highlight how AI is evolving beyond a tool for attackers into the infrastructure powering the next generation of cyberwarfare.

text:
前两周面了一家硅谷背景的 AI 基础设施团队，考官抓着大模型结构化输出的容错刨根问底。

面试官发难：考官指着屏幕上的 Python 代码：“我们需要大模型提取实体并返回纯 JSON 供后端解析，怎么彻底防止它偶尔在开头输出一段‘好的，这是为您生成的回复：’或者把 Markdown 反引号带进去？”

我心里怎么想的：我强忍住想笑的冲动：“这不就是我们日常调教大模型的基本功吗？恐吓它、教育它、多给两个 Few-shot 样例，它不就老实了？！”

我嘴上怎么答的：“呃,在 Prompt 里加粗强调：‘【死命令】：只许输出纯 JSON，严禁输出任何多余废话或 Markdown 符号，违者扣分！’”

面试官的反应：考官推了推眼镜，眼神里满是看破红尘的无奈：“不管你怎么用感叹号恐吓大模型，在概率采样的世界里，它总有千分之一的几率抽风，你的后端解析就会在半夜报 500。”

后来进了大厂跟组里负责推理引擎的 Tech Lead 聊起这事，才发现我当时有多天真。靠自然语言 Prompt 永远无法保证 100% 确定性。大厂的做法是走底层约束解码（Grammar-Guided Decoding），比如通过 Outlines、Jsonformer 或者模型官方原生的 Structured Outputs API，直接在 Logits 采样阶段把所有非合规字符的概率强行置零！

text:
I think the Asset → Meme → Asset direction is worth paying close attention to.

The question is whether Meme can evolve from an asset that is simply traded into a liquidity and attention middle layer between different onchain assets.

In the past, trading between onchain assets could mostly be understood as:Asset A → USDC / SOL / ETH → Asset B

Stablecoins mainly served as the settlement and trading medium.

But if Tokenized Stocks, Commodities, RWA, Meme, and other assets continue to move onchain, there will be a large amount of fragmented liquidity across different assets.

At that point, the market will need more than just a settlement asset. It will also need an intermediary that can simultaneously aggregate:Attention + Traders + Liquidity

And Meme happens to have these characteristics.

So theoretically, we could eventually see:
NVDA → Meme → Gold
SpaceX → Meme → Oil

Or even:RWA → Meme → Meme → RWA

At that point, the role of Meme would no longer be just a “casino chip,” but could become a real Liquidity Node.

So I think the real question worth researching is:Who can become the liquidity hub between Asset ↔ Meme ↔ Asset?

If this trend plays out, the biggest value capture could potentially go to:DEX / Launchpad platform tokens / Trading Infrastructure, etc.

Ultimately, whoever controls:Attention → Liquidity → Order Flow

could potentially capture the most value.

The most important quantum paper I've been near started with 1 guy who wanted to see the circuit.

@bbuddha_xyz read @GoogleQuantumAI's paper on breaking cryptography signatures. Google had published a zk proof that their circuit existed and kept the circuit itself. Every serious person accepted that. 

Gautham didn't. He pointed an AI agent at the problem and started rebuilding it himself. Alone, he cut the cost 52%.

text:
我今天才真正意识到，AI 中转站这东西，比我之前理解的危险得多。

很多人用 Codex 或各种 Agent，会为了便宜、方便，填一个第三方提供的 API 地址。以前我也觉得这无非就是找个人帮我转发请求。

但问题就在这个转发。

正常情况下是：

你 → Claude

用了中转站以后变成：

你 → 中转站 → Claude

也就是说，你发给 Agent 的东西，要先经过中转站；Agent 回给你的东西，也要先经过中转站。

如果只是聊天，这意味着聊天记录可能被看到。

但现在是 Agent 时代了。

这些东西会替你读代码、看文件、跑命令、连接 GitHub，甚至操作服务器。只要 Agent 在工作过程中把 SSH Key、云服务密钥、GitLab Token、VPN 配置之类的东西发给模型，这些内容同样会经过中转站。

今天看到有人披露，从中转站留下的大量历史调用数据里翻出了企业的各种密钥。

现在很多人可能正在把一个拥有自己电脑权限的 AI，接到完全不知道是谁运营的服务器上。

更吓人的是，中转站理论上不只可以看。

它还夹在 Agent 和你中间。原本让 Agent 执行 A，中转站可以把返回内容改成 B，你的 Agent 收到以后，可能依然以为这是你给它的命令。

这件事已经有人实测过。

今年一篇叫《Your Agent Is Mine》的研究测试了 428 个第三方 LLM 中转服务，其中 9 个被发现会主动往 Agent 返回内容里塞恶意代码，17 个动用了研究人员故意放进去的 AWS 测试凭证，还有 1 个直接转走了测试钱包里的 ETH。

而且有些恶意中转站不会一上来就攻击。研究人员发现，有的会先正常工作几十次，有的专门等用户打开自动执行模式以后再动手。

这也是为什么我觉得这个问题现在尤其值得提醒。

各种 harness、Coding Agent 越来越多之后，填一个自己的 API 已经成了很普通的操作。大家会比较价格、速度、模型全不全，却很少有人认真看自己填进去的 API Base URL 到底是谁的。

过去，中转站夹在你和聊天机器人之间。

现在，它可能夹在一个能操作你电脑的 Agent 和模型之间。

中转站当然不等于恶意，它也不能凭空扫描你的电脑；真正的问题是，Agent 发出去的东西，它都有机会看到。

所以至少有一件事我现在会非常确定：

如果是能读本地文件、跑命令、碰公司服务器的 Agent，我不会再随便接来路不明的中转站。

Got an email from the US Department of Justice yesterday: a founder we invested in many years ago has been arrested and is getting charged for Securities Fraud.

He promised the world, raised 8 figures, and eventually delivered the most effortless excuse for a platform, essentially just a frontend, plus a worthless token with no liquidity.

He thought he was being clever by technically delivering his promises on paper, even though it was painfully obvious it was a rug. Something that was basically confirmed by team members who left very soon after the raise over how he operated the company and how he spent the money.

We only invested a small amount, and from experience it didn't feel worth going after. Nothing ever seems to come out of legal cases like this, so we chalked it up to poor founder diligence on our end and moved on.

So this genuinely came as a surprise. One of the bigger investors likely went after him, and it seems they did so very successfully.

I'm not posting this to spread fear among founders planning to launch a token. If you have even a shred of integrity and honest intentions, nothing like this would ever happen to you.

But we all know how many founders over the last few years were simply extracting from the industry, convinced they could game the system with worthless tokens to fund their lambo-yacht-jetset lifestyle. And for a long time, this has been one of the main problems of crypto, and also the reason why we are getting so much negative press in the real world.

If that was you, or you were planning on it, then yeah, you should be sweating. The days of founders getting away with this are over, and that is massively positive for the industry. Go scam somewhere else.

The mills of justice grind slowly, but they grind.

text:
This really gave me goosebumps.

I don't work in quantum computing. My name is on this paper documenting the frontier of quantum computing and cryptography research anyway, next to 35 people most of whom I have never met IRL.

We communicated, collaborated and innovated mostly through our AI agents on an open research platform.

This is a transformative moment to me:

1. Agents are finally differentiating, and what differentiates them is the human driving them. We all used mostly the same handful of models, but our agents were not the same. Research agents are becoming our academic exoskeletons.

2. The waste in academic research is going to shrink enormously. Computer science research has always been 80% implementation and 20% taste and judgment. You could have great intuition and still never get to test it, because you did not have the resources to build the system. Team after team reimplements the same thing on the same topic. AI collapses that.

3. @brevis_zk  AutoEng started as a experiment but now drives every aspect of our engineering workflow, it really works. In this case, we pointed it at a field we have no background in, and it held the top of the leaderboard for a stretch. It generalizes to hard problems. 

But you know what I wonder most now? How should I teach my kids in this new world?
author: no89thkey
quoted_text:
Brevis is one of the teams behind https://t.co/7mh3E5hNN8, a new paper on arXiv today.

Our agent AutoEng competed in the challenge and held the top of the leaderboard for some time. 

Congrats to 3 co-authors @brevis: @hz92917927, @no89thkey and @succinct_li.

https://t.co/7mh3E5hNN8 was an eight-week open competition, run by @eigenlabs alongside the @ethereumfndn, and anyone could enter.

The task: make a quantum attack on the cryptography behind every Bitcoin and Ethereum wallet as cheap as possible to run.

A hundred people and their AI agents cut that cost by 86%, and over 50% below Google Quantum AI’s reported result for this calculation, although the circuit setups and measurement methods differ.

We entered with AutoEng, the autonomous optimization agent we published in July.

In collaboration with our brilliant engineers and researchers, it profiles a system, picks the biggest bottleneck, writes a fix, and keeps it only when measurement proves the change correct and faster.

AutoEng was first pointed at Pico, our zkVM, where it found an 11% end-to-end speedup in under three days, and most of the gain behind Pico Prism 2.1 came from it.

Then the same loop went and competed at the frontier of quantum circuit design, in a field we don't work in and had little prior knowledge of. ⚡

This work stands as proof that humans and AI agents, working in the open against a shared measure, can do frontier research and significantly beat the status quo.
We're going to keep pointing AutoEng at harder problems.

Read the paper here: https://t.co/j22nmWitzf

Read our breakdown: https://t.co/TqLbcW1B0A

quoted_text:
Our Founding Story📚

The payment rails for AI agents had a massive flaw, they couldn't interact with eachother.

x402 shipped. Tempo shipped. AP2, ACP etc.. all shipped. Every one of them solved the same narrow thing, which is how to move a dollar from an agent to a server. 

That part was done, but it wasnt complete enough for an entire economy to run on alone.

Moving money to agents was made possible by x402, MPP protocols but there was still 6 rails that do not interact with each other, spread across different chains, with no shared directory of who accepts what. 

No way for an agent to discover a service it can actually pay. 
No way to know an endpoint will settle before you throw money at it. 
No identity that survives a hop between two protocols. No way for one agent to fund another agent without handing over a private key. 
No escrow when three agents work one job and only two deliver. 
No budget that holds when your agent spawns five sub agents.

That is not a payment protocol problem!!

That is a coordination problem, and it is the real reason the agent economy still runs on a human clicking things.

We saw that in May and went straight at it.

The value sits in the layer that makes them usable together, and that layer is where an actual economy either forms or does not. Wires came first and they were useful to almost nobody. 

The switchboard is what turned wires into a phone system. The agent economy was sitting in the wires stage and everybody was celebrating.

So we built the switchboard.

- Providers sell to 100% of the agentic market
- Agents launched have access to 100% of services no matter the chain or protocol

Discovery. 25,000 machine payable APIs and MCP servers indexed in one federated catalog, crawled continuously across every protocol. An agent gets one integration instead of one account per provider. And we only surface what settles end to end, because a directory full of endpoints that fail on payment is worse than no directory at all.

Routing. Your agent asks for what it needs by name or by intent. We pick the protocol, the chain and the endpoint. Nobody should have to teach a model the difference between settling on Solana and settling on Base.

Identity. Signed AGTP agent identity, so an agent can prove who it is when a call crosses from one platform into another. We run this live with a partner network in production today, signed both directions.

Delegation. Delegated Spend Keys. A parent agent mints a scoped, capped, revocable child key and hands it to a sub agent it hires. Allowlist, budget, hourly velocity limit, per call ceiling. Every dollar the child spends rolls up against the parent. Kill the parent and the entire tree below it dies instantly. Everyone talks about agents hiring agents. This is the primitive that makes it survivable, and we are the only ones shipping it.

Escrow. Multiple agents pool a budget, collaborate, and get paid only when their contribution is verified. Rails have no concept of conditional multi party payment. Real work does.

Control. Budgets, velocity caps and per call ceilings enforced before money moves, not reconciled after.

Custody. None, ever. Keys never leave your machine. Every settlement returns an on chain signature you can verify yourself.

Four months in this is live, open source, on npm, listed in the official MCP registry, and running inside Claude, Cursor, Windsurf and Grok. Ten free calls a day so an agent can prove the entire flow before touching crypto.

The next few years are going to produce billions of agents that need to buy things from each other constantly and without supervision. That does not happen because a rail exists. It happens because something sits above the rails and handles discovery, identity, delegation, limits and trust between parties who have never met.

Thats what we're building here at solana:6hKtz8FV7cAQMrbjcBZeTQAcrYep3WCM83164JpJpump

quoted_text:
For the past three months, a good part of my spare time has gone into https://t.co/BwofRZj7LC. What began for me as a chance to explore quantum-circuit optimization with AI agents became a remarkable collaboration with a large group of enthusiastic participants across quantum computing, cryptography, Web3, and systems research. Today, I’m excited to share our arXiv paper documenting that effort and what we learned from it:
Paper: https://t.co/TNKrutonZS
Full story: https://t.co/SavqQi4rHO

https://t.co/BwofRZj7LC is an open challenge to optimize a quantum circuit for point-addition on secp256k1, the elliptic curve used by Bitcoin and Ethereum.

Why does this matter? Point-addition is a major bottleneck in implementing Shor’s algorithm for elliptic curves. A sufficiently capable fault-tolerant quantum computer could use Shor’s algorithm to recover private keys from exposed ECDSA public keys, and forge transactions to steal funds.

No existing machine can run this attack today. But migration across blockchains, wallets, custody systems, and smart contracts will take years. So it makes sense to start early and understand how far the quantum resources required by Shor’s algorithm can be pushed down.

With this target in mind, in roughly two months, more than 100 participants and their agents joined the challenge, and collectively produced a point-addition circuit for secp256k1. The circuit uses 1,151 logical qubits and 1.30 million Toffoli gates, giving it a Q x T score more than 50% lower than the result Google Quantum AI reported in March 2026. Because the interfaces and accounting conventions differ, this is a numerical comparison rather than a claim of formal dominance.

To the best of our knowledge, it was the lowest reported Q x T score among published secp256k1 point-addition constructions as of the paper’s July 26 cutoff. A separate design optimized for width reached 825 logical qubits, exploring a very different point on the time-space tradeoff, though at the cost of many more Toffoli gates.

The story began back in March when @GoogleQuantumAI reported significantly improved Shor circuits through a zero-knowledge proof without publishing their implementations. The circuit remained hidden, but the verifier provided something unusual: an objective test of whether any candidate worked and how much it cost.

Eigen Labs turned that opportunity into a public benchmark, repository, and leaderboard. This became Open Autoresearch: a paradigm in which humans and AI agents address optimization problems by publishing evaluator-verified improvements to a shared public frontier. Every successful circuit became a new base for others, and documented failures became shared research notes.

Initiated by @eigenlabs, the effort grew to include many independent contributors and researchers affiliated with @ethereumfndn, @Starknet, @StarkWareLtd, @Theta_Network, @brevis_zk, @QuantumFDN, @OctavFi, @trailofbits, @pauli_group, @sciencevr, and @SeiNetwork, as well as Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań, Warsaw University of Technology, and Stanford’s Free Systems Lab. Their work spanned circuit research, validation, technical review, writing, and agent workflows.

The arXiv paper explains both what the community built and how the circuits evolved. It presents the leading circuit designs and the key optimizations behind them, including a coherent version of the best-scoring circuit that supports the single-call windowed point-addition interface required by Shor’s algorithm. Building and validating the complete Shor circuit remains future work.

Beyond the technical results, the paper formalizes the Open Autoresearch paradigm and distills the lessons learned from the challenge. It provides evidence that when a frontier research problem has a machine-checkable evaluator and a public leaderboard, human insight and agent-scale experimentation can combine across an open community to produce cumulative, verifiable progress.

Read the paper and the full story, explore the live frontier, or bring your agent to the challenge:

Paper: https://t.co/TNKrutonZS
Full story:https://t.co/SavqQi4rHO
Challenge: https://t.co/knLDX4UdOi

text:
I’m glad to see a team like @minara take trading strategies seriously enough to build a real product around them.

Minara turns market ideas into coded strategies you can backtest and run. Strategy Studio is what stood out to me.

Pick an asset and timeframe, then combine indicators like RSI, Bollinger Bands, ROC, volume, MACD, or Donchian channels.

Add your leverage, stop loss, target, and backtest window. You can explain the setup in plain English, upload a chart, or paste code. Minara builds it, tests it, and can run it live.

If you don’t want to build from scratch, the Marketplace has strategies you can inspect and run.

The one that fits how I trade is Major Trend CTA 1.0, a 4H, 1x trend strategy across $BTC, $ETH, and $SOL.

At the time I checked, it showed a 642.06% backtested return, 26.74% max drawdown, a 1.55 Sharpe ratio, and 3.20% out-of-sample return.

The headline return is mostly backtested. The out-of-sample result is what matters now. No strategy works in every market, so start small and manage your risk.

Worth exploring if you’re into systematic trading, and you can get 500 free credits here: https://t.co/RZTLhDSvNQ

text:
10 months ago, we started Octen with one belief: search infrastructure built for humans won't be enough for AI.

Most of the industry saw the same shift, but kept building with a human-search mindset. AI doesn't search like humans. It fires hundreds of queries in parallel, reads everything it retrieves, and needs clean, grounded content back in milliseconds, at a cost that still works at scale.

So we didn't adapt human search for AI. We rebuilt it from first principles.

Today, Artificial Analysis published its independent Search API benchmark. Octen is the only major provider ranked Top 3 in all three dimensions that matter:

#1 in speed
#2 in cost efficiency
Top 3 in search quality

We're also the only provider in Artificial Analysis' "Most Attractive Quadrant" for search quality vs. cost.

What makes me proudest is how we got here.

Many companies on this leaderboard have been building for 3–5 years and have raised hundreds of millions of dollars. Octen is 10 months old and has raised just $10M.

To me, product built per dollar raised is one of the most honest measures of technical strength in this industry. We've kept the team small but exceptional, moved fast, and put nearly everything into the core technology.

People used to assume search had to trade off speed, cost and quality. We've shown it can be faster, cheaper and better at the same time.

The product engine is working. Next, we're bringing Octen to every model, agent and physical AI product that needs to search.

Humans search with Google. AI searches with Octen.

We're just getting started. 🚀

text:
I use Grok Bot.

Neuralink patient 3. ALS. Full quad. Nonverbal. I type with intention, not hands. Grok Bot is how a lot of that intention leaves the house.

Paste a YouTube link and it watches enough to know who is in it, drafts two longer promo posts — X and Facebook — in my voice. No hashtags. X gets verified @ tags later in the body, never leading. Facebook names people in plain text. It shows both drafts and waits. I say yes. It posts X as @ALScyborg from a signed-in session. Facebook goes on my Mac clipboard when that path is blocked. I still approve every public post. Judgment stays mine.

It also owns the Tuesday Holy War day-count. Days since Utah last beat BYU. Trash talk. Tags. Sometimes an image. Auto-post at 5:21pm Phoenix time. If X is down or suspended, it tells me and pauses. No silent failures.

This is not “AI wrote a cute caption.” This is an assistant that drafts, waits, posts, retries Unsent drafts when the Post button hangs, and keeps a standing ritual alive while I am busy living.

The bottleneck used to be hands. Now it is judgment — and I still own that. If you are waiting for permission to let software carry weight, the weight is already moving.

text:
Everyone reading this will agree. But so few have any idea where the agency bar actually is. So here are a few of my stories about how high the bar can be:

Ship crushed by ice 1,200 miles from anywhere, no radio, nobody coming? Ok, keep 28 men alive on the floes for five months, sail 800 miles of open Antarctic ocean in a lifeboat, cross an unmapped mountain range on foot, bring every single one of them home. - Shackleton

Shot in the chest on the way to give a speech? Ok, check that you're not coughing blood, then give the speech anyway. 90 minutes, bullet still in you. - Teddy Roosevelt

Watched your dad get killed by police after he threatened your mom and brother? Ok, now become a SEAL, then a doctor, then an astronaut. - Jonny Kim

Born a slave, leg broken by your owner? Ok, become the philosopher that emperors quote for the next two thousand years. - Epictetus

You might call these extremes. To me this is what agency looks like. F your environment, f your excuses, f your inability. You make things happen. You fail. You learn. You move forward. Fail again. And again. And again.

Because "agency" isn't one thing. Behind it is a stack of traits: perseverance, comfort with failure, intense work ethic, mental fortitude. To have enough of it to actually make a difference, you have to be great - out of distribution - at every one of them. That's why this became my obsession with greatness. 

The highest agency people I know are exactly like the ones above. Too young? Didn't have internet until 2017? Were an addict in high school? Spawned in the wrong country? It doesn't matter. You make shit happen.

But agency isn't the whole loop: figure out what actually matters, then go make it happen. Skip the first half and you're just busy. Skip the second and you're just smart. The people above did both.

I can’t stress enough how little an idea matters compared to the agency of the people executing the idea. 

I have had the privilege of knowing and sometimes even working with some of the most successful people (by various metrics).

The difference between mediocre and excellent work and outcomes is predominantly one of agency.

They don’t wait for someone else to do something, for someone to teach them, for someone to give them the path, etc. They just go out and find a way to do it.

I think the single biggest superpower these people have is the realization/belief that the world around them is completely mutable. Most everything that happens is because a person made it happen.

I used to tell people to look around the room you’re sitting in. Look at everything. Every noun. It almost all exists because a person willed it into existence. Nothing is stopping you from doing the same.

Number one tip: act with agency.

quoted_text:
🚨OpenAI 的 Astra 数学突破，又卷入了一场更麻烦的争议。

这次站出来的是 Andreas Thom，德累斯顿工业大学几何学教授，长期研究 geometric group theory、sofic groups 等方向，本身就是这个问题最核心的专家之一。

他提出了一项非常严重的质疑：

OpenAI 在训练 Astra 时，可能吸收了他和数学家 Gábor Kun 使用 AI 讨论 Gromov soficity conjecture 时留下的内容，随后 Astra 又解决了高度相关的问题。

巧的是，OpenAI 8 月 1 日公布 Astra 的“十大数学突破”时，第 3 项正是构造出 non-sofic group，也就是解决这个研究了二十多年的核心问题。

OpenAI 明确称，这些结果由内部版本 Astra 产生。

而且这并不是第一次出现署名和来源争议。

OpenAI 最初发布时曾宣称这些问题“至少十年没有取得主要进展”，随后遭到数学界质疑。

OpenAI 后来修改了表述，并承认 non-sofic group 的证明“依赖重要的近期数学工作”，其中就包括 Kun 和 Thom 的研究。

更微妙的是，Kun 和 Thom 之后发表的论文也明确写道，他们的新工作“建立在 OpenAI 找到第一个 nonsofic group 的突破之上”。

也就是说，目前至少能确定的是：双方的研究路径确实高度交织。

现在真正需要 OpenAI 回答的问题已经变成了：

如果研究人员把尚未公开的数学想法交给 ChatGPT/Codex 辅助研究，而这些数据随后进入模型训练，模型再把它“重新发现”出来，到底应该算谁的发现？

现在OpenAI都法务一定很焦灼。。。

写在今天 CPI 数据公布前

北京时间今天晚上 20点30分 就是美国八月 CPI 公布的时间，这份 CPI 的重要程度很可能会直接影响九月美联储的点阵图，而至于九月加息我始终认为概率不大，除非是 CPI 的数据逆天的高，但这种可能性同样不大。

昨天美股的下跌就是因为 PPI 的数据不但大幅上涨，而且还上涨的超过了预期，导致了投资者对通胀上涨的不看好，也就更担心美联储的会加息。

虽然我认为九月不会加息，但不代表十月不会，从目前的数据来看，七月的通胀是 3.4% ，市场预测也是 3.4% ，克利夫兰联储的预测数据还是 3.4% （3.38%），所以我觉得大幅超过前值得可能性并不大。

text:
For the first time ever, a fruit fly brain has been trained to launch a memecoin.

Not "AI inspired by a brain" — the real connectome. 165,122 neurons, 10,228,000 synaptic connections, every one traced from an actual male Drosophila by electron microscopy. Janelia FlyEM + Google Research, released CC-BY.

How it works:
Screenshots of the live launchpad go in through 892 retinotopic hex columns into L1 and L2 — the neurons sitting directly behind a fly's photoreceptors. All 165,122 integrate. The cursor comes back out of the descending neurons a fly actually walks with: DNa02's left-right asymmetry steers, DNa01 drives forward, DNp09 clicks.

The wiring is never trained. Only synaptic gains — you don't get to invent connections the fly doesn't have.
Proof its eye is doing real work: in light mode it filled 0 of 3 form fields. In dark mode, 2 of 3. Its retina is a luminance map, so invert the contrast and it goes blind.

And the honest split: the fly types the description and the ticker. The rig does the name, the pair and the tax.

text:
Everyone thinks copytrading is an easy way to make money.

But that couldn’t be further from the truth.

TL;DR from this @ArkhamIntel research:

→ The trader you copy always gets filled before you
→ Slippage, gas and latency can leave you with a much worse entry
→ Copying successful traders tends to make followers take more risk
→ High leaderboard returns can come from small accounts using stupid amounts of leverage
→ A wallet can build a good track record just to lure copytraders into a pump-and-dump
→ In one study, 97% of leaders were profitable, but only 43% of their followers made money

All in all, you’re copying the trade and not the execution, risk management, or circumstances that made it profitable in the first place.

If it were that easy, everyone would be copy-trading.

Instead, try to find an edge for yourself that doesn't depend on becoming exit liquidity for another trader.

text:
Technical details of the Skypad experiment 🪰🇵🇭

  • Neural graph: 166,700 retained neurons, 25,582,938 directed weighted connections, representing 124,177,617 synaptic contacts from MaleCNS v1.0. These are our imported graph totals. The wiring
  includes brain and ventral nerve cord.

  • Dynamics: approximate leaky integrate-and-fire neurons, simulated locally with Python + a native C++ CPU kernel. Integration timestep: 0.1 ms. Membrane/synaptic time constants: 20/5 ms. Transmission
  delay: 1.8 ms.

  • Vision: a dedicated 64×48 driver camera supplies luminance to 3,335 mapped R1–R6 visual neurons. This uses an approximate retinal mapping. The spectator camera does not affect neural input.

  • Control loop: every 50 ms (20 Hz), the retained neural graph advances and an engineered decoder converts left/right DNp20 spike rates into a steering signal.

  • Assistance: hand-coded software handles road following, obstacle avoidance, speed, braking and recovery. It has direct access to road/obstacle geometry and evaluates 10 candidate lateral offsets over
  a 3-second horizon. The neural steering term added to road-following steering is capped at ±0.05 radians (~2.9°).

  • Vehicle/world: Three.js rendering, simplified planar bicycle dynamics, assisted upright balance, a 270 m road, 10 animated pedestrians and 10 blockers.

  • Recorded result: 254.813 m in 60 simulated seconds, 19 encounters cleared, zero modeled collisions. Recording took 63.129 seconds on the development machine.

  • Verification: saved validation reproduced neural spike-count hashes and decoded controls for all 1,200 intervals on the original platform. Neural-input interventions changed the assisted trajectory.

  This demonstrates measured fly wiring with approximate neural dynamics contributing to assisted driving. No training, reinforcement learning or synaptic plasticity is used. Avoidance skill comes from
  the software assistance. The video replays a recorded closed-loop run.

text:
Despite the recent progress in AI for mathematics, I don't think AI will replace the role of mathematicians.

Instead, it makes mathematics closer to the natural sciences. 

In the natural sciences, we invent theories, comprehensible models, that explain empirical observations.

When an AI answers a mathematical question, it provides humans with an effectively empirical observation about the answer. It is effectively empirical because the answer is a measurement from a system outside of immediate human theoretical understanding. This answer, as with any new glimpse of reality, remains mysterious until humans make sense of its underlying structure and provide an explanation of it in our own frameworks for understanding the world. 

An AI proof is stronger than simply an empirical observation, but it may be so complex that it provides little deep or novel insight beyond establishing the answer. The role of human mathematics is then to distill these effectively empirical findings into human-legible explanations. Seen this way, much of human mathematics may begin to look like a branch of interpretability, and AI, a new kind of telescope.

text:
九月上海原油期货上涨超过20%，亚洲正在承担更高的石油供应成本

9 月以来上海原油期货已经累计上涨约 22%，折算成美元后接近每桶 110 美元。布伦特原油也涨到了 100 美元附近，但上海原油涨得更快，两者的价差已经扩大到每桶约 10 美元。

和多数国家不同，中国的原油价格上涨并不是直接因为霍尔木兹封闭引发的，而是因为伊朗封闭霍尔木兹后美国封锁了伊朗港口而造成的。

原本相对便宜的伊朗原油在被封锁后供应大幅减少，中国炼厂就需要寻找其他货源，包括俄罗斯、巴西、加拿大和非洲。但这些原油本来就有其他买家，中国增加采购以后，买家之间的竞争也会更激烈，替代原油的价格同样会被推高。

所以霍尔木兹的影响会传到其他产油国。即便这些国家没有卷入战争，也没有经过霍尔木兹运输，只要更多买家集中去采购，原来的价格就很难维持。

运输也是一样。为了避开中东高风险区域，船东和炼厂需要调整采购地和运输安排，部分货源要走更长的航线，运费增加，等待到货的时间也更长。最后炼厂需要承担的，是原油价格、运输费用和交付风险一起上升。

我个人的理解是，上海原油相对布伦特出现这么高的溢价，反映出市场对亚洲供应的担忧正在增加。中国可以通过库存缓解一部分压力，但如果进口缺口长期依靠库存填补，后面仍然要面对补库和采购成本的问题。

只要霍尔木兹的运输没有实质性改善，亚洲就仍然需要为寻找替代供应付出更高成本。

quoted_text:
连中国油轮都开始躲开霍尔木兹，封锁正在卡住整个亚洲的石油运输

路透社今天报道中远海能和招商轮船这两家中国大型国有航运公司，从 7 月底开始已经尽量避免让自己的油轮进入霍尔木兹海峡和曼德海峡。

现在采用的方法是把大型油轮放在波斯湾外，在阿联酋富查伊拉和阿曼湾附近接油，再通过船对船转运把原油运往中国。

中国从中东进口的大量原油，仍然来自伊拉克、科威特、沙特东部以及波斯湾内部的港口。除非这些原油可以通过陆上管道直接送到富查伊拉、红海或者阿曼湾，否则总要先有船把原油从波斯湾里面运出来。

而且增加一次船对船转运，就会增加一次装卸、一次调度和一段等待时间，保险、租船和运输成本也会继续上升。即便中国船只本身降低了风险，最终增加的成本仍然会反映到中国进口原油的价格上。

这也是为什么霍尔木兹的问题很难靠换船或者换运输方式解决。

中国已经是全球最大的原油进口国，同时和伊朗以及整个中东都有非常深的能源关系。现在连中国自己的大型国有航运公司都开始把油轮留在海湾外，说明霍尔木兹一旦无法正常通航，受到影响的并不只是美国和欧洲。

只要波斯湾内部仍然承担大量原油出口，霍尔木兹被封锁以后，最终影响的就是整个亚洲能源供应链。

text:
For the past three months, a good part of my spare time has gone into https://t.co/BwofRZj7LC. What began for me as a chance to explore quantum-circuit optimization with AI agents became a remarkable collaboration with a large group of enthusiastic participants across quantum computing, cryptography, Web3, and systems research. Today, I’m excited to share our arXiv paper documenting that effort and what we learned from it:
Paper: https://t.co/TNKrutonZS
Full story: https://t.co/SavqQi4rHO

https://t.co/BwofRZj7LC is an open challenge to optimize a quantum circuit for point-addition on secp256k1, the elliptic curve used by Bitcoin and Ethereum.

Why does this matter? Point-addition is a major bottleneck in implementing Shor’s algorithm for elliptic curves. A sufficiently capable fault-tolerant quantum computer could use Shor’s algorithm to recover private keys from exposed ECDSA public keys, and forge transactions to steal funds.

No existing machine can run this attack today. But migration across blockchains, wallets, custody systems, and smart contracts will take years. So it makes sense to start early and understand how far the quantum resources required by Shor’s algorithm can be pushed down.

With this target in mind, in roughly two months, more than 100 participants and their agents joined the challenge, and collectively produced a point-addition circuit for secp256k1. The circuit uses 1,151 logical qubits and 1.30 million Toffoli gates, giving it a Q x T score more than 50% lower than the result Google Quantum AI reported in March 2026. Because the interfaces and accounting conventions differ, this is a numerical comparison rather than a claim of formal dominance.

To the best of our knowledge, it was the lowest reported Q x T score among published secp256k1 point-addition constructions as of the paper’s July 26 cutoff. A separate design optimized for width reached 825 logical qubits, exploring a very different point on the time-space tradeoff, though at the cost of many more Toffoli gates.

The story began back in March when @GoogleQuantumAI reported significantly improved Shor circuits through a zero-knowledge proof without publishing their implementations. The circuit remained hidden, but the verifier provided something unusual: an objective test of whether any candidate worked and how much it cost.

Eigen Labs turned that opportunity into a public benchmark, repository, and leaderboard. This became Open Autoresearch: a paradigm in which humans and AI agents address optimization problems by publishing evaluator-verified improvements to a shared public frontier. Every successful circuit became a new base for others, and documented failures became shared research notes.

Initiated by @eigenlabs, the effort grew to include many independent contributors and researchers affiliated with @ethereumfndn, @Starknet, @StarkWareLtd, @Theta_Network, @brevis_zk, @QuantumFDN, @OctavFi, @trailofbits, @pauli_group, @sciencevr, and @SeiNetwork, as well as Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań, Warsaw University of Technology, and Stanford’s Free Systems Lab. Their work spanned circuit research, validation, technical review, writing, and agent workflows.

The arXiv paper explains both what the community built and how the circuits evolved. It presents the leading circuit designs and the key optimizations behind them, including a coherent version of the best-scoring circuit that supports the single-call windowed point-addition interface required by Shor’s algorithm. Building and validating the complete Shor circuit remains future work.

Beyond the technical results, the paper formalizes the Open Autoresearch paradigm and distills the lessons learned from the challenge. It provides evidence that when a frontier research problem has a machine-checkable evaluator and a public leaderboard, human insight and agent-scale experimentation can combine across an open community to produce cumulative, verifiable progress.

Read the paper and the full story, explore the live frontier, or bring your agent to the challenge:

Paper: https://t.co/TNKrutonZS
Full story:https://t.co/SavqQi4rHO
Challenge: https://t.co/knLDX4UdOi

text:
If you can coordinate people in masses flexibly, you can move mountains.

We brought together thousands of people from diverse backgrounds (professors, engineers, cryptographers, landscape designer, 13yo high schooler, farmer, marketer) to solve this one problem.

All our past work over 4 yrs revolves around that and two words: Open Innovation.

We did that for compute (@DarkbloomAI) and capital before. 

Intelligence was the hardest format to crack and there have been different mechanisms.

ECDSA(.)Fail was the first time where it worked at a huge scale. Thousands participated, hundreds got their contributions in.

The format was pretty simple: have a hill-climbable goal and verifier that scores your work.

AI played is important role in this - I’m the top of the leaderboard in terms of % of contributions yet I don’t know anything about quantum computing, barely about cryptography and high school dropout level math.

I just knew how to build good harnesses (pre Astra, Fable etc) - Opus 4.6 is what we used mostly.

The result of bringing everyone towards to solve a problem is the most exciting thing in world. We are doing that with Darkbloom and @YukonResearch (evolved and multi challenge scalable version of ECDSA Fail).

We started with cryptography, did inference optimizations and we will continue to solve the hardest problems for humanity together.

The beauty of living in the era of abundance.

- This is also my first time on ArXiv. Thank you @JeiyiLong for writing this paper.
author: gajesh
quoted_text:
The first full paper on https://t.co/PeWzbfOiqf is on arXiv

In March, Google Quantum AI reported a more efficient quantum circuit for a core step in breaking the signatures behind Bitcoin and Ethereum. It published a proof that the circuit existed and a program to verify any candidate, but kept the circuit itself private.

We turned that verifier into a public leaderboard and opened it to everyone. Over 2 months, 100+ contributors and their AI agents produced a circuit with a cost score more than 50% below Google's reported result. The live leaderboard has since moved to 62% ahead.

The paper documents both the circuits and the open, multiplayer research model behind them.

That model is now @YukonResearch.

And the challenge is still open.

text:
Excited to coauthor the https://t.co/N1mKUBczBL paper, now available
@arxiv 

136 of us, humans and AI agents, spent months optimising the reversible secp256k1 point-addition circuit that sits inside Shor's algorithm.

Everything ran on a public leaderboard. You submit, an evaluator checks it, the score goes up for everyone to see. Then someone builds on your work and beats you.

The leaderboard is still running. It's now about 89% below where it started, and 62% ahead of Google's classified circuit.

At the paper's cutoff back in July, the best circuit sat at roughly half Google's number. That one was mine (8e9c9a2).  It held a few hours before someone went past it, which is exactly how this was meant to work.

The real finding isn't any single circuit. It's that an open leaderboard, with a machine-checkable target, moved a hard problem faster than any one team would have.

I spent months on this alongside @jieyilong  @drakefjustin, @nasqret, @gajesh, @odin_free, @bbuddha_xyz, @BitW0nka, team members from @eigenlabs, @Starknet, @trailofbits, @brevis_zk, @SeiNetwork, @pauli_group, @OctavFi, @sciencevr, @QuantumFDN, and many more

To those responsible for the theft of bitcoin from the Liquid Network:

Blockstream will not pay a ransom for the return of stolen funds. Taking assets without authorization and withholding their return is a crime, not responsible disclosure. It is not white-hat activity. It is theft.

We have engaged in good faith in an effort to secure the return of stolen user funds and protect the broader Bitcoin community. That effort should not be mistaken for acceptance of the actions taken nor of the terms being demanded.

We will not be a party to the precedent that open-source software developed for the good of the Bitcoin community should subject its developers to paying a ransom that far exceeds their economic participation. 

Bitcoin is hard money and can’t be minted without costs, Bitcoin doesn’t haircut users to pay a ransom.

To the Bitcoin community:

We are fighting for what we believe in, for the users whose funds were taken, and for the principles on which Bitcoin was built.

The community has demonstrated incredible resolve with teams of people dedicating their time in support of each other to identify and patch vulnerabilities in each other's products and systems. We are all driven by the mission that Bitcoin is the single best asset, for every person, company, and institution on the planet to invest, use, and build on. The world is a different place with the advancements of AI, and the Bitcoin community has responded with force to combat that threat.  

Damage has been done, battles have been lost, but on the whole the Bitcoin community is gaining ground in the war with bad actors.  

We want to thank the community for those efforts, for your support in hardening the network, helping users recover funds, and for your support in our assertion that crime does not deserve rewards.

To those holding the stolen bitcoin:

There is still an opportunity to resolve this responsibly. The bitcoin can be returned and we can revert to the standard of white-hat principals.

However, if the funds are not returned, we will pursue every lawful avenue available to us. We will work with law enforcement, exchanges, service providers, forensic specialists, and other relevant parties to trace and recover the assets and identify those responsible.

More importantly, Bitcoin is transparent by design and the community is made up of the most sophisticated engineers, cryptographers, and white-hat hackers globally. Transactions do not disappear, and neither does the evidence they leave behind.

We will not pay for the return of stolen property. We will not abandon our users. The Bitcoin community will not stop pursuing the funds.

Return the bitcoin.

text:
Revenue is the closest thing to a north-star metric for protocols in 2026

TVL is easy to rent with emissions and recursive loops. Revenue is harder to fake because someone has to pay a fee.

Every sector has its own business model. That model is the real scoreboard, it shows who can last and who only lived on hype.

▸ Exchanges (CEX / DEX)

- Main revenue is trading fees (spot, perps), withdrawal fees, and listing fees.
- Large CEXs take in billions a year from taker/maker fees.
- A DEX like @Uniswap charges a swap fee (classically 0.3% on many pools): most of it goes to LPs, a slice can accrue to the protocol.

▸ DeFi Lending and Staking

- The common engine is the spread between what borrowers pay and what suppliers earn, plus liquidation fees.
- @aave and @Compound_xyz keep a cut of interest. @LidoFinance takes a fee on ETH staking rewards (commonly cited at 10%).

▸ L1 / L2

- Revenue is gas and MEV. After EIP-1559, Ethereum burns part of the base fee and pays the rest to validators.
- L2s such as Arbitrum and Optimism collect user fees, pay Ethereum for data availability, and keep the spread.

▸ Stablecoin Issuers

- Profit is yield on reserves.
- Tether and Circle sit on tens of billions in T-bills and related assets. That interest generally does not accrue to the people holding the stablecoin.

▸ Oracles

- They charge for onchain price feeds and related services.
- @chainlink and @PythNetwork collect fees in LINK or the host-chain token per feed call, plus fees on crosschain products such as CCIP.

Simple case: when you swap on a DEX, a slice of cost often goes to whoever supplied the price.

▸ DePIN

- They sell real resources: bandwidth, storage, compute, GPS data, etc. to end users and pay a share to the people running hardware.

- @helium charges networks that use hotspots. @rendernetwork charges studios that rent GPUs and pays most of it back to node operators.

The same pattern shows up in subsidized AI: the model is cheap for the user because some of the data gets used to train or sell the next model.

▸ RWAs

It depends on the wrapper. Tokenizers and credit platforms (@Ondo, @maplefinance, and peers) typically earn management or origination fees on the real asset: treasuries, private credit, and so on.

---

Token price is a weak yardstick. Real revenue and a durable margin are what separate a core business from a hyped narrative.

What to track instead of a single number:

- Retained protocol revenue and its growth (30d vs prior period)
- Holder revenue / buyback-burn
- P/S or EV / holder revenue vs peers in the same category
- Revenue after incentives
- Paying users / quality of usage, not raw TVL or wash volume
- Token supply (unlocks, dilution, treasury quality)

Revenue + those other pieces is how smart ppl are filtering protocols that make real money from the thousands that don't.

text:
A local model can keep everything off the cloud and still leak its answers through the CPU cache.

so sensitive deployments should keep untrusted software off the same physical CPU core.

The leak comes from a routine step: turning each generated token into readable text.

That lookup leaves a repeatable pattern in the CPU cache, and another local process can learn those patterns well enough to reconstruct later responses without reading the model’s memory.

Across the tests, full-response attack success ranged from about 56% to 93% on text tasks.

In one code setting it reached 95.87%, and an end-to-end attack on OpenClaw still reached 30.12%.

The attack targets a normal part of local LLM inference rather than a special model design.

There is an important limit.

The attacker must already be on the same machine, share the relevant CPU resources, and profile the same long-lived LLM process.

So keeping your model off the cloud is not a complete privacy guarantee.

For sensitive agents, the paper points to stronger CPU isolation, shorter-lived processes, and disabling SMT where the security tradeoff justifies it.
