author: varun_mathur
quoted_text:
For the past three months, a good part of my spare time has gone into https://t.co/BwofRZj7LC. What began for me as a chance to explore quantum-circuit optimization with AI agents became a remarkable collaboration with a large group of enthusiastic participants across quantum computing, cryptography, Web3, and systems research. Today, I’m excited to share our arXiv paper documenting that effort and what we learned from it:
Paper: https://t.co/TNKrutonZS
Full story: https://t.co/SavqQi4rHO

https://t.co/BwofRZj7LC is an open challenge to optimize a quantum circuit for point-addition on secp256k1, the elliptic curve used by Bitcoin and Ethereum.

Why does this matter? Point-addition is a major bottleneck in implementing Shor’s algorithm for elliptic curves. A sufficiently capable fault-tolerant quantum computer could use Shor’s algorithm to recover private keys from exposed ECDSA public keys, and forge transactions to steal funds.

No existing machine can run this attack today. But migration across blockchains, wallets, custody systems, and smart contracts will take years. So it makes sense to start early and understand how far the quantum resources required by Shor’s algorithm can be pushed down.

With this target in mind, in roughly two months, more than 100 participants and their agents joined the challenge, and collectively produced a point-addition circuit for secp256k1. The circuit uses 1,151 logical qubits and 1.30 million Toffoli gates, giving it a Q x T score more than 50% lower than the result Google Quantum AI reported in March 2026. Because the interfaces and accounting conventions differ, this is a numerical comparison rather than a claim of formal dominance.

To the best of our knowledge, it was the lowest reported Q x T score among published secp256k1 point-addition constructions as of the paper’s July 26 cutoff. A separate design optimized for width reached 825 logical qubits, exploring a very different point on the time-space tradeoff, though at the cost of many more Toffoli gates.

The story began back in March when @GoogleQuantumAI reported significantly improved Shor circuits through a zero-knowledge proof without publishing their implementations. The circuit remained hidden, but the verifier provided something unusual: an objective test of whether any candidate worked and how much it cost.

Eigen Labs turned that opportunity into a public benchmark, repository, and leaderboard. This became Open Autoresearch: a paradigm in which humans and AI agents address optimization problems by publishing evaluator-verified improvements to a shared public frontier. Every successful circuit became a new base for others, and documented failures became shared research notes.

Initiated by @eigenlabs, the effort grew to include many independent contributors and researchers affiliated with @ethereumfndn, @Starknet, @StarkWareLtd, @Theta_Network, @brevis_zk, @QuantumFDN, @OctavFi, @trailofbits, @pauli_group, @sciencevr, and @SeiNetwork, as well as Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań, Warsaw University of Technology, and Stanford’s Free Systems Lab. Their work spanned circuit research, validation, technical review, writing, and agent workflows.

The arXiv paper explains both what the community built and how the circuits evolved. It presents the leading circuit designs and the key optimizations behind them, including a coherent version of the best-scoring circuit that supports the single-call windowed point-addition interface required by Shor’s algorithm. Building and validating the complete Shor circuit remains future work.

Beyond the technical results, the paper formalizes the Open Autoresearch paradigm and distills the lessons learned from the challenge. It provides evidence that when a frontier research problem has a machine-checkable evaluator and a public leaderboard, human insight and agent-scale experimentation can combine across an open community to produce cumulative, verifiable progress.

Read the paper and the full story, explore the live frontier, or bring your agent to the challenge:

Paper: https://t.co/TNKrutonZS
Full story:https://t.co/SavqQi4rHO
Challenge: https://t.co/knLDX4UdOi

text:
今天偶然刷到这篇文，必须分享下，尤其开头第一段

众所周知我一直Bullish RWA，尤其是资产（美股，黄金，大宗）代币化这条线，之前就写过我第一个买入的山寨是2017年的比原链

不过之前我更多是从下面三个角度思考

1. 我个人，以及全世界很多类似散户，有通过稳定币购买各种美元资产的需求

2. 美国政府可以通过美元稳定币的输出扩展美元霸权，体量足够大的时候甚至可以帮助化债。美股代币化则是美元资产输出到全球的最佳方式

3. 代币化美股可以实现“扩权”，让股票在分红和投票之外拥有更多更有意思的功能与玩法

而这篇文章是从一个我之前没有想到的角度切入的 - 资产负债表

核心思想就是 - 整个金融业因为资产的“包装”形态所产生的摩擦是巨大的，代币化是一个非常好的Solution

第一段我直接翻译一下放在这，方便大家理解

“
代币对资本市场的影响，将如同集装箱对全球贸易的影响一样。

金融业面临着一个成本高昂的“包装”问题。每项资产都有其自身的包装，并运行在各自的操作系统中：抵押贷款包含一系列合同、PDF文件、数据库和服务关系；私募股权基金的权益包含一份认购协议和过户代理人电子表格中的一行记录；股票的流通涉及经纪人、托管人和存管机构的记录链。这样的例子不胜枚举。

这些资金虽然存在于世界各地的资产负债表上，但如果没有专门的操作流程，其中大部分资金仍然无法在机构间自由流动。这种摩擦减缓了资本重新部署到新企业、基础设施、住房和其他生产性用途的速度。

当资产在不同机构间流动时，通常需要进行拆解、核实、协调，然后再重新整合到接收机构的系统中。之所以存在这么多工作，很大程度上是因为不同机构对同一基础资产和权益持有不同的表述。在全球范围内，这种碎片化给社会带来了巨大的隐性成本：几乎1.8千万亿美元的资产

代币化从根本上解决了这个问题。代币为资产或金融债权提供了一个标准化的、机器可读的接口。一旦资产能够在共享网络上被识别和使用，交易所、贷款机构、托管机构、服务商和软件应用程序就可以与它们交互，而无需每次都重建金融堆栈。最终，这将构建一条通往在通用可编程轨道上运行的资本市场的道路——在这个市场中，资产的流动、结算和应用将更加顺畅。

用容器化来类比代币化将如何改变世界，效果最佳。
”

text:
Had something very similar happen to me a few months ago.

With AI scams getting this convincing, here are 5 rules everyone should follow to avoid getting scammed ↓

1. Have a family safe word for emergencies and unexpected money requests.

2. Hang up and call them back yourself using the number already saved in your phone.

3. Caller ID & familiar voice prove nothing. Phone numbers, names, and even voices can be easily spoofed.

4. "Urgent" "Don't hang up" "I need this asap" = the most obvious red flags. Urgency makes you panic and stop thinking rationally.

5. Keep your family information like names, relationships, vacations, schools, employers, etc. 
More context =  more material for scammers to make impersonations convincing.

Yesterday, a film accusing Israel of genocide premiered.

It’s a horrific blood libel against our sons and daughters. What makes it especially painful and infuriating is that this lie comes from Israeli filmmakers and is now being spread around the world.

Let’s get the facts straight:

On October 7th, Hamas invaded Israel to murder Jews. Hamas terrorists slaughtered children in front of their parents and parents in front of their children. They burned homes, raped women, and kidnapped babies, children and elderly people.

Then Hamas fled back to Gaza and deliberately hid behind its own civilians, using them as human shields in homes, schools, and hospitals.

And when Israel fights back, and civilians are tragically killed in this terrible war, Israel is accused of “genocide.”

There is no magic button that can destroy Hamas, or any terrorist organization hiding behind civilians, without harming a single civilian. It simply does not exist.

In interviews with the international media, I always ask: “What would you do?”

They never have an answer.

If Israel wanted to hurt the people of Gaza, we would not send our sons and daughters to fight house to house, through alleyways and tunnels, at the terrible cost of our own soldiers being killed and wounded.

We would not warn civilians before strikes and evacuate them from combat zones.

We would not help vaccinate hundreds of thousands of children in Gaza against polio.

The war in Gaza is terrible. The death of every child is a tragedy.

But a terrible war is not genocide.

Even now, Hamas doesn’t regret October 7th. It’s rearming and waiting for another opportunity to carry out a massacre.

The people standing between us and that next massacre are our soldiers and reservists. Our sons and daughters who put their lives at risk so that we can live here safely.

I love them.
I am proud of them.
And I am deeply grateful to them.

To portray them as perpetrators of “genocide” is not courageous art.

It is a cowardly blood libel.

And I will not remain silent.

the overreaction to this tweet from the STONK community is crazy work tbh

apparently i'm only allowed to buy one launchpad token ever

trying to buy another one apparently means i'm trying to PvP the sector leader

and i find this even funnier because the #2 solana:6GmAFSYs4gk3FDao5FzzySQpPZaWsa4rUJHacpMpUNgx holder bought $EMBER at a $2.8m market cap, holds a lot of it, and has been bullposting it for days

no one cared

but the moment i buy $EMBER at ~6x the valuation he did, i'm suddenly the villain

different rules apply for me i guess!

for the avoidance of doubt:

i am bullish on solana:6GmAFSYs4gk3FDao5FzzySQpPZaWsa4rUJHacpMpUNgx

i vocally praised it in a post days ago despite having 0 exposure, and that post has now done 400k+ views

i also explicitly said that Solana leadership rallying behind solana:6GmAFSYs4gk3FDao5FzzySQpPZaWsa4rUJHacpMpUNgx is by far the biggest reason i've turned bullish on the Solana ecosystem again after being mostly bearish for months

i legitimately think solana:6GmAFSYs4gk3FDao5FzzySQpPZaWsa4rUJHacpMpUNgx will do very well

and if you believe in its long-term vision, this entire overreaction creating a dip should probably be viewed as an entry, not a reason to panic

so why didn't i buy?

simple:

my trading style has always been low caps where i believe the asymmetry is better

i very rarely buy large caps, even when i think they're going to perform well

that's just how i trade

and honestly, the community coming up in arms over me buying $EMBER is bullish for solana:6GmAFSYs4gk3FDao5FzzySQpPZaWsa4rUJHacpMpUNgx in its own way

it shows there is a genuine cult behind it

and in crypto, you almost never go wrong betting against a cult

but the idea that me buying another meme/stock launchpad token is somehow an attack on solana:6GmAFSYs4gk3FDao5FzzySQpPZaWsa4rUJHacpMpUNgx because there is already a sector leader is ridiculous

this is like saying nobody should buy the Meteora token because Raydium and Jupiter already have tokens

that makes absolutely zero sense and is actually antithetical to the whole idea of crypto

there can be multiple winners in the same sector

as i've said to several people in the comments since my $EMBER purchase:

i have ZERO PvP intent

i still think STONK will do well

i'm rooting for it to do well

but there is room for multiple projects to win

the idea that there can only be one project of a certain type in crypto, and everyone MUST buy that one project and nothing else or they're the spawn of the devil, is fundamentally anti-crypto

competition is good

multiple winners are good

and if anything, this entire episode has made me even more bullish on the strength of the STONK community

This week’s Robinhood–AMC dispute over tokenized stock is really a debate about who gets to say yes to access.

@CEOAdam argues the issuer should decide. We’re more aligned with @vladtenev: if a company is public, its shares are already part of a market designed for broad participation. Tokenization shouldn’t give issuers a new veto over how that market evolves.

The bigger issue is what we believe tokenization is actually for.

If the goal is simply to put existing financial assets on new rails, then the old gatekeepers remain intact, just now with better infrastructure. 

But if tokenization is supposed to change financial markets, then it has to change who can participate in them, how they participate, and who gets to determine the terms of that access.

As our co-founder @ARafayGadit put it:
“Tokenization’s biggest prize isn’t faster settlement for the already included. It’s access for everyone else.”

That’s a point we've been making for a long time now.

Because the question isn’t whether tokenized stocks are technically possible.

It’s whether the next generation of markets will be built to expand access or whether we’ll simply recreate the same boundaries, permissions and gatekeepers that exist today, onchain.
author: ZIGChain
quoted_text:
Everyone should be able to access high-quality financial assets, wherever they live.

That's what tokenization unlocks: taking the best of US capital markets and making them available on a global scale.

The industry is still small compared with global finance, but the advantages are becoming harder to ignore. Traditional market infrastructure was built around fixed hours, closed networks and layers of intermediaries. It was never designed for 24/7 execution, programmable assets, composability or self-custody.

The needs of investors have moved faster than the rails underneath them. We're working to change that.

What gives me confidence is seeing how many different people are now pushing this industry forward. Founders are building new products, LPs are bringing liquidity, traders are finding new uses, and infrastructure teams are making the whole thing work.

It's a privilege to be in the trenches with all of you.

We are still early, and there is a huge amount left to build. It will also take time and effort for the old guard to get onboard. This is worth fighting for.

text:
Cloudflare enabled ML-DSA-44 validation on 1.1.1.1 yesterday. No other major public resolver has announced equivalent support. I wrote an analysis because this is the strongest practical PQC migration case study I have seen this year. And it shows nicely why PQC migration is a systems engineering problem, and not just a library swap. One resolver deployment surfaced three problems that every protocol relying on digital signatures will face:

- A 2,420-byte signature exceeds the 1,232-byte DNS/UDP ceiling, forcing TCP fallback on every post-quantum DNSKEY fetch 

- Dual-algorithm coexistence creates a downgrade path that current DNSSEC validation rules do not prevent

- The chain of trust from root to leaf must migrate end to end, and neither ICANN nor Verisign has announced a post-quantum root signing timeline

The organizations treating PQC migration as a library swap will discover these constraints one protocol at a time, usually in production. DNS, TLS, X.509, IKEv2: each protocol breaks differently when signatures grow by a factor of 38. This announcement made all three problems visible.

https://t.co/DIpmuqQNZn

text:
@saylor using chatgpt to create $STRC is the first example of AI hallucinating a novel financial structure into existence which now operates at >$1B scale, and it’s only the beginning

Financial innovation is about to have its cambrian explosion, driven by superintelligence & programmable trust on Ethereum. Structures no human has ever conceived can now be proposed by machines, enforced by a network, and tested by markets continuously at global scale

Every financial contract ever written is a bundle of state-contingent claims on who pays whom, how much, when, and in which states of the world. The most fundamental claim types such as lending, insurance, and equity have existed for ~4,000yrs since Hammurabi. The payoff space is well-trodden

All financial innovation since, all the way to today, has built on top of the same payoff space and comes from either (a) an evolution in imagination of emergent, system-level properties or (b) a step-function unlock in feasibility. Many are both and one bound always clears last

AI takes the former to its theoretical limit via hallucination, exhaustive state space traversal & simulation, and DeFi takes the latter to its theoretical limit via low-overhead instantiation of arbitrary structures & programmable trust

Imagination

Humans search a small region of the design space, are path-dependent, and generally converge on local maxima over a much longer timeframe. This also explains why so much of what passes for financial innovation is either a new way to lever debt, obscure risk, or perform ratings arbitrage. AI can traverse the space exhaustively in real-time and invent structures or mutations in regions of the design space humans would never think or dare to explore. It also searches across many domains at once - it can pull mechanisms from auction theory, insurance, biology and distributed systems that no financial engineer was trained in. Finally, it can simulate a structure's emergent, system-level behavior before a dollar is actually deployed, where humans historically discovered those properties by running the experiment on the real economy

A good historical example of this category is fractional reserve banking - this is just lending + pooling + a demand option but it went unconceived for well over ~1,000 years and now underpins modern credit creation and economic growth through its emergent property at the system level. Bitcoin is also a great example - compute, networks, Merkle trees, hashcash, and ECDSA cryptography existed around 2000 but Bitcoin only materialized in 2008. AI raises attempts by orders of magnitude at a constant or better hit rate

Feasibility

A financial contract is viable when the following inequality is satisfied:

cost of verifying the trigger + enforcing payment + coordinating parties < value transferred

An instrument can be imagined and economically desirable long before it becomes practical to implement. The set of possible structures that clear that inequality expands every time verification, enforcement, or coordination becomes cheaper 

On Ethereum, protocols of arbitrary complexity can be instantiated with zero overhead costs via smart contracts, inherit programmable trust by outsourcing enforcement to the network rather than intermediaries and lawyers, capital and counterparties operated by humans and now AI agents can assemble around a structure immediately once it becomes live, and the network's public state becomes something you can write contracts against. This enables cheap real-time instantiation, growth, rapid iteration, and evolution of arbitrary structures. Distributed ledger technology is a step-function unlock across all the properties to the left of the inequality and can birth a new universe of systems that were previously not feasible. Early instances of this are flash loans and AMM's which made liquid markets for any asset viable

A good example in the feasibility category is mortgage-backed securities - they were tried in the 1880s and again in the 1920s and collapsed both times. They only worked in 1970 via Ginnie Mae once mortgages became standardized enough to pool, could be guaranteed enough to trust, and computers could track thousands of loans at once

---

Both bounds are falling at once- AI expands the structures we can discover, DeFi expands the structures we can actually execute and scale. When the cost of inventing a structure and the cost of making it credible collapse at the same time, the rate of experimentation will go parabolic. Most will fail, but a few will become entirely new species of primitives

@3janexyz we believe that a significant share of the primitives that will dominate finance a century from now have not been invented yet and many that do survive will be unrecognizable in their current form

I encourage the ten remaining builders in DeFi to revisit their priors about whats possible now that superintelligence is at your fingertips and build something that has never existed. Start world-building

text:
🚨 On September 6, 2026, @Liquid_BTC was affected by a cache key collision vulnerability in rangeproof verification.

An attacker minted ~3,998.5 L-BTC with no corresponding peg-in. Within minutes, the unbacked L-BTC was pegged out into real BTC on the Bitcoin mainnet. About 3,400 BTC was later returned to the federation peg wallet, while ~598.5 BTC remains under the attacker’s control.

The SlowMist Security Team traced the fund flows on the #Bitcoin side using @MistTrack_io and fully analyzed the incident.

🧩 Attack flow:

1️⃣ Two setup transactions first landed valid rangeproofs and commitments, while embedding a crafted payload in the locking script to seed node caches.

2️⃣ A follow-up minting output reused a colliding cache key — the same raw concatenation of proof, commitment, asset commitment, and scriptPubKey, but with different field boundaries.

3️⃣ On a cache hit, nodes skipped secp256k1_rangeproof_verify and min-value checks, accepted an unbacked commitment, and minted ~3,998.5 L-BTC. The fake UTXOs were consolidated and pegged out within minutes.

⚙️ Root Cause: The Elements rangeproof cache key concatenated variable-length fields without length prefixes. Distinct argument tuples could hash to the same key, so a positive cache hit meant skipping cryptographic verification.

🛡️ SlowMist Insight: A positive-result cache in a consensus verification path is itself a cryptographic primitive. Every field the verifier reads — and every field boundary — must be unambiguously bound into the key. Treat cache-key integrity as a mandatory item in consensus-layer audits.

Full analysis👇
https://t.co/4wntCFawfb

另一方面，开始定价加息，长端利率短期走弱+原油价格回落，反而给风险市场获得了短期的喘息效果，但是此时并不能过分乐观，一旦市场逐渐对加息完成定价，长端利率与2年收益率继续呈现出上涨趋势，风险市场还是要遭受挤压，并且原油价格也并未回归安全区间

美股盘前的反弹，或者开盘后的小幅度反弹，对于高Beta股票，我认为是下周加息前一个不错的反弹减仓的机会

quoted_text:
原油价格下行，9月加息概率走弱，进一步的油价下跌能否对冲今晚CPI带来的预期影响？

今晚的CPI算是9月议息会议前的“最终审批”，数据公布前因为国际原油价格短期下挫9月加息概率降低至67.1%

很明显，今晚CPI虽然作为主要观察数据，但是原油价格依旧是一个核心变量，可以对今晚的CPI影响力放大or对冲减弱的效果

今晚的CPI数据详细拆解不多说，可以看图片，除了关注对9月加息概率的影响之外，还要关注服务业，住房以及能源的二次传导，这是作为详细研究来关注的，作为大多数小伙伴来说，关注数据本身即可

图片中我列出了三种可能出现数据组合，从最好到最差，在原油价格不变的前提下，将会直接影响9月加息概率

最好数据组合，削弱9月加息概率，大概率可以回归45%-55%区间，

中性组合，9月加息概率大概率会维持在65%-80%附近，但是要看详细数据中，商品，能源二次通胀以及服务业的情况，细则数据影响概率向上还是向下

最差组合，直接推高9月加息概率突破80%甚至到90%，

原油价格依旧是核心变量，目前原油价格已经提前降低了一部分9月加息概率，但是这种跌幅不够，原油价格想要真正进入缓和乐观阶段，恐怕要Brent跌破95，WTI跌破90才能达到这种效果，否则对今晚数据影响只能是放大利空or利多以及对冲作用

关注今晚数据组合之后还要看原油价格是放大利好/利空，还是对冲，至于加息概率的变化对市场的影响，可以参考图二

我们自己认为9月是否加息可能只会影响个人的交易判断与仓位调整，但是概率上依旧不能忽视，尤其是概率一旦突破70%进入80%甚至90%，市场必然做出相应的反应

傻逼的共识也是共识，错误的共识也是一样，一旦概率提升，意味着预期形成共识，哪怕像我依旧不觉得沃什敢加息，但是依旧做好一定的防御与仓位调整！

Sample DMHC notice language (small group employer, 14-pt for key lines):

"The Department of Managed Health Care has determined that the premium rate increase for this product is unreasonable or not justified after reviewing information submitted to it by [plan].

This means that the plan did not provide enough information to support the rate increase or the rate was found unjustified or unreasonable for other reasons. You can keep your current plan product, choose a different plan product, or look for other coverage. Small group purchasers may want to contact Covered California..."

Yes, contractholders (employers) are explicitly told they can switch to other coverage or keep it. The finding does not void the contract or block the rate, but enables exit by not renewing under it.

text:
🚨 US CPI: Inflation Comes In Hotter Than Expected

August US inflation data delivered a firmer-than-expected headline reading, adding another complication to the Federal Reserve outlook.

Headline CPI rose 0.396% M/M on an unrounded basis, effectively 0.4%, compared with expectations of around 0.39%.

The bigger surprise came from core CPI, which increased 0.290% M/M, versus expectations of around 0.22% and up from 0.215% in the previous month.

On a year-over-year basis:

Headline CPI: 3.397%
Core CPI: 2.446%, down from 2.478% previously

The composition is important. Headline inflation is running above 3%, while monthly core inflation accelerated materially. That combination makes the path toward easier monetary policy more difficult, particularly against a backdrop of elevated energy prices and geopolitical risk.

写在今天 CPI 数据公布前

北京时间今天晚上 20点30分 就是美国八月 CPI 公布的时间，这份 CPI 的重要程度很可能会直接影响九月美联储的点阵图，而至于九月加息我始终认为概率不大，除非是 CPI 的数据逆天的高，但这种可能性同样不大。

昨天美股的下跌就是因为 PPI 的数据不但大幅上涨，而且还上涨的超过了预期，导致了投资者对通胀上涨的不看好，也就更担心美联储的会加息。

text:
truly the end of an era to see shopify move away from react native.

back in 2018, we moved coinbase to RN. app quality was worse, but it let us keep teams lean and avoid the platform tax of building twice. also, some of the best engineers i knew were working on making it better and the trendline seemed promising..

fast forward to 2020, and it was hard to tell react native apps apart from native ones. meta, expo, shopify, software mansion, and many others had made the tooling and ecosystem so much better.

the absolute killer feature was over-the-air updates. you could ship major updates instantly without app store reviews, which made mobile development as fast and fluid as building for the web.

it was a godsend for us, since apple's reviewers were capricious with crypto apps. even coinbase, a licensed exchange, got kicked out of the app store for several weeks. having ota updates meant freedom from the tyranny of the reviewer.

by 2024, things got interesting. meta and others were rewriting core parts of their apps in native code for performance, with react native serving as the shell that bound it all together. rn's new architecture was also a really brutal upgrade. we spent weeks on it and got bogged down by dependency and performance issues. it was a pretty heavy tax to pay, and many never made the upgrade. so the gap between fully react native apps and native apps continued to grow.

it's the age of llms now, and we chose to build a react native app this year but the choice was not an obvious one anymore. 

the ota part is still very valuable, but the platform tax is dropping every day with agents, and it seems feasible to have fast-moving, lean teams that can build for both ios and android.

sad to see, but react native usage will probably reduce slowly over the next few years.

text:
I was booked on United Flight 93 on 9/11, 2001, flying nonstop from Newark NJ to San Francisco CA. Around midnight the night before, a coworker called me urging me to change my flight to fly into San Jose instead. This meant I had move to a flight that boarded 20 minutes later (from the same gate) with a stopover in Denver.  I was very reluctant to do it but I did. 

When I got to the airport, I watched people boarding flight 93 and I was upset that I was not leaving earlier, in my 1st class seat on a direct flight. I didn’t notice or care about the people as they were boarding, only myself.  

When I finally boarded my plane, we were 7 planes behind flight 93. When we were 3 planes away from we taking off, the pilot told us to look out the right side of the plane because it appeared the Twin Towers had been hit by a plane. I thought it might have been a small Cessna until I saw the second plane strike the other tower. We were grounded just before taking off. 

I changed that day. I now take every opportunity I have to watch and if possible, get to know the people I’m boarding a plane with. I never hesitate to give up my seat for a later flight if requested. I’ve had two children since 9/11 and went to multiple mission trips to war torn countries. Every day I wake up breathing is another gift from God. 

Never forget 🇺🇸🇺🇸🇺🇸

text:
🧠 An agent finds a listing announcement. What happens next?

PrivateAI has already faced this question while developing the Research Agent.

Several articles may describe the same event using different names. One mentions the company, another names its product, and a third refers only to the market or research area. The agent needs to understand that these texts belong to the same story.

❗️This is what the Semantic Layer helps with.

In simple terms, the Semantic Layer sits between the documents and the agent. It helps the agent select relevant information and connect references that describe the same company, product or event.

A future trading agent would need similar context. If it finds a post about an upcoming listing, it must identify the correct token, trace the post back to its source, distinguish a new announcement from an old repost and check whether the market has already reacted.

PrivateAI already uses this approach to process information with the Research Agent. In future releases, we can explore how the same context could support agents working with TheThing core terminal.

text:
TLDW from yesterday's stream with @flexmeow @omgcorn and @johnnyonline_

- Flex is a fixed rate money market on @yearnfi where borrowers set their own rate. liquidity is managed through redemptions instead of utilization curves

- if a lender wants liquidity back, they trigger a redemption. it sells the borrower's collateral for the borrow asset and cuts their debt by the same amount. this means no utilization spikes and no liquidations from liquidity crunches. the redemptions clear from lowest rate up, so paying more insulates your position

- no spread means markets can run at 100% utilization. borrowers pay x% + collateral, lenders earn x%, nothing eaten by a curve

- this also makes Flex great for illiquid/semi liquid collateral like locked yvUSD, LSTs, RWAs (stuff that sometimes gets wrecked on morpho/aave when a 2-week unlock meets a rate spike); Flex just redeems it in kind instead of forcing a fire sale

- tradeoff: not great for directional looping like long ETH against USDC, since getting redeemed at the wrong time is basically forced deleveraging at a bad price

- roadmap: v1.1/v2 brings in kind redemptions for locked collateral markets, more non-Yearn assets, and an immutable token where lockers get 100% of protocol revenue

- feedback from the hosts: clean design, real respect for the risk tab being front and center instead of buried in docs. Bauti suggested a non-curated entry point for advanced users, and needing more assets before the risk profile broadens past heavy loopers

Yep. Except:

1. This was about important internal tools. The team was stuck in some architecture nightmare of their own doing (writing it in rails but headless, with graphql api, and a SPA react app, constantly needing frontend engineers for changes). I call this kind of thing 'cosplaying an enterprise production app'. All that complexity was in the way and using straight rails was perfect in that case.

2. I make calls like this all the time. Usually someone on the team asks me to. They see what needs to happen but don’t want to be the bad guy. I’m happy to just make the call if I agree with the premise. Saves enormous amounts of meetings and change management etc. Sometimes this is jokingly referred to as Founder-mode-as-a-service here.

3. For ten years I’ve also run an internal podcast called Context, where I revisit decisions like these and explain the reasoning so everyone can learn from them. This is helpful to give people all the variables that were considered and why this was the choice made given the information available at the time. I want to teach how to make such decisions effectively without needing me. Sunk cost fallacy is a problem.

4. Any notions that Shopify is succcessful despite of me doing this, instead of because of it, will have a hard time making their argument come together I think 😄

the part of 'two weeks later tobi learns about...' is nonsese and the pivot of that project up there happens one of the more successful examples of interventions. But getting the company to work effectively with great architecture and low technical debt baggage into the right direction is literally the job, so guilty as charged I suppose.

But there are always cope stories floating around like this because they are more fun, than saying 'somehow we needed tobi to stop doing silly architecture astronautics'.  I can totally see that.

author: lex_node
quoted_text:
I just published a new paper exploring the operational, financial, and business benefits of permissionless blockchains as compared to permissioned networks for activities such as payments and capital markets.

It lays out how permissionless systems like Bitcoin and Ethereum offer desirable properties such as resilience, diminished counterparty risk, and guaranteed settlement. These benefits are endogenous to the system: what regulators and users see is what they get.

It then describes the mechanical reasons why the reintroduction of a gatekeeper in permissioned networks forfeits these benefits. Such networks can never be as reliable and are more vulnerable to cyberattack, particularly in the age of AI. Their guarantees are exogenous and live inside off-platform agreements.

My paper argues permissioned networks are not blockchains and the assets they hold should not be considered tokens. Their consensus and cryptography are mostly performative.

Lastly, my paper describes an oft-missed business benefit of permissionless systems: the inability of incumbents to take them over and exercise monopoly power, in the way they historically have in TradFi. 

Permissioned networks are destined for the same fate, which is why they should be avoided by smaller entities (like community banks) and startups.

My argument relies on the decades-old literature in distributed consensus, current statistics on network reliability, and the first principles of TradFi design for clearing and settlement.

I wrote it because I think it’s important for lawmakers and regulators to start distinguishing between the two designs. Thinking the two types of platforms are similar opens the door to dangerous regulatory arbitrage.

Now is the time to understand the difference from a technical, financial, and practical point of view. 

So take a look and let me know what you think ⬇️

text:
Im not convinced people actually know what the P=NP problem is.

Lets break it down. 

Before the 1960s, computers were getting faster every year, so engineers just assumed that if a problem was too hard for a computer to solve then, all had to do was just wait a few years for a faster computer, boom, problemo solved. 

But then, they ran into a wall with a specific group of problems. No matter how powerful the computers got, they would freeze up, overheat, or take billions of years to solve them. 

So these were super hard theoretical physics or black hole topography, right? Nope, they were everyday things like designing a high school schedule where a teacher is never in two places at the same time, or like, draw a trace on a circuit board that's as short as possible without overlapping other traces.

Heres the kicker, once the problem was solved, the computer could VERY quickly go back over and be like "Yup, no scheduling conflicts!". Once the problem was solved, verifying the solution was easy. It would be like you walking up to a lock someone left on a door and trying to figure out the code, and then someone else coming up behind you "Hey, the code is 26-42-36-10. Pop in the code and boom! Problem solved, solution verified. 

Computer scientists grouped all of these problems into a category called "NP". Aww now if makes sense. And you know what ALLLLLLL of these problems have in common? They were exponential. Meaning if you only had 5 classes, your computer could solve thay in a MILISECOND. But if your schedule had like 100 classes, the possible combinations went insane like, more atoms than in the known universe numbers.

So by putting these problems into this "NP category", scientists were basically telling software developers "Stop wasting billions of dollars on trying to get your computers to solve these problems" and do something heuristic like, draw a line first, then verify it sux and iterate on it quickly until its good enough and move on. 

So then they realized something terrifying. If you could figure out a trick to solving ANY of these problems, you could solve ALL of them, no matter what it was as long as it was an NP problem.

Ok so whats the big deal then!?! What do people mean why they say "If AI solves P=NP, thats the end game!". They are essentially saying that if its easy to verify a solution to a problem that was solved, then there must be a hidden trick to solve it as easily from scratch and if you could find that trick, all the hard problems could be solved instantly. Some of this is good like medicine or cosmology, some of it bad like cryptography  which rides on assumptions that these problems are extremely difficult to solve from scratch. 

Thats the entire breakdown on the P=NP or P≠NP debate you see floating around X these days.

Thanks for reading.

quoted_text:
Here’s my thesis on HYPE’s price over the next few months, keeping it as rational as possible.

How do we do that? By focusing on revenue.

We know more and more TradFi players are getting involved in $HYPE. These players value stocks using P/E ratios and I think that’s exactly how $HYPE is being valued. It isn’t trading like any other major or revenue-less altcoin like $ZEC etc. Otherwise, we’d already be at $300 given all the insane news we’ve had so far.

With that in mind, here’s my thesis:

I still believe there will be another airdrop. And I’ll keep believing that until the team changes the tokenomics, which explicitly state that the community will be rewarded again.

Based on that, I’m estimating the next airdrop at around 6–8% of the total supply, worth roughly $6–8B at $100. Of that $8B, I expect a decent chunk to be used as collateral to borrow USDC. Somewhere between $1B and $2B in borrowing doesn’t sound unreasonable to me.

That would mean at least $2B in USDC being minted on Hyperliquid, before even accounting for people who simply sell instead of borrowing. We could potentially reach $10B in USDC held on Hyperliquid pretty easily.

$10B in USDC would generate $314M in annual revenue (almost 50% more revenue on top of the roughly $700M annualized we’re doing right now).

Then there are the CEX integrations: Kraken, Coinbase, and probably others. Those integrations would bring more people trading on HL which also means more USDC held on HL.

That could easily take us to $15–20B, depending on the integrations and how much traction they get. That doesn’t seem far-fetched at all.

At $20B we’d be looking at $628M in additional annual revenue, almost doubling what we’re generating today.

While $HYPE has been pricing in some of this revenue growth over the past few weeks, imo it’s only pricing in the USDC already held on HL.

On top of that, we’d have trading fees from users accessing HL through CEXs. That could be huge too.

It’s hard to estimate, because we know CEXs heavily fake their reported volume, liquidation, and other stats. But Hyperliquid averaged $8B in daily trading volume over the year, including around $7.7B in perps and $320M in spot.

Doubling that really doesn’t seem like a stretch with Kraken and especially Coinbase. And that’s before any other major exchanges join the party.

If volume doubles, assuming the same effective fee rates, trading fee revenue would double too. That would put us at $1.3–1.4B in trading fee revenue + $1B from AQAv2, for a total of $2.3–2.4B in annual revenue (roughly 3x what we’re generating today).

We could also add HIP-4 revenue if it takes off and starts generating meaningful fees, along with priority fees, which could scale massively (particularly from arbitrage between HIP-3 star order books and the standard order books on HL.

But even without those last two factors, we’d already be looking at roughly 3x current revenue.

That’s why I think $HYPE could easily hit $200 over the next few months, driven by these integrations alone, without needing market euphoria or an absurdly inflated P/E ratio.

And I’m not even talking about long term price targets, with HSI very likely to keep accumulating supply, the Assistance Fund doing the same and so on.

You’re not bullish enough.

Hyperliquid.

text:
Pearl, Nockchain and Dolphin are all being sold as "verifiable AI" right now. I asked each one simple question: what exactly gets verified? The answers are different, and it changes everything. Table below.

Start with what a buyer of inference wants to know. You send a request to a stranger's GPU. Did the model you paid for answer it, or something smaller and cheaper? That is the whole problem. Everything else is marketing.

Pearl answers a different question: did someone do expensive matrix math? It swapped Bitcoin's SHA-256 for matmul and proves the work with a tiny ZK proof. The cryptography is excellent. But the protocol accepts any matrices, and @abhinaba_ai June study (arXiv 2606.04819) showed random matrices with no model attached still earn rewards, and the dominant mining software has no AI code at all. Real inference mining exists (Together AI runs a Pearl-mined endpoint), but it's the minority. And even then, the proof is about a block, not your request.

Nockchain gets closer. Its Lockstep paper makes a GPU server and a CPU reference produce identical bits at near stock speed. Serious work, but a paper released this week: closed engine under NDA, H100 only, audits switched off, not part of consensus. What's live is a matmul mining puzzle with Pearl's gap: it proves math happened, not that it served anyone.

Small note: Both Pearl and Nock are heavily (pre-)mined by team. No real fair launch. Nockchain launched in 2025 as "programmable gold," pivoted to privacy during the ZEC run, rebranded as a proving market in April, and is now AI compute. Four identities in 16 months. 

@dphnAI is the only one verifying what a buyer cares about, on a live network.

Validators send signed, one-time challenges that sample the model weights actually loaded in a node's memory while it answers, and check them against the approved model. About 0.1% overhead, never touches your prompt. Output fingerprinting and performance bounds sit on top. New operators must mine four weeks of earnings into a slashable bond before withdrawing anything, so there's no window to cheat and run.

It does this on idle gaming GPUs, where bit-for-bit verification isn't possible today. So Dolphin checks model identity directly, checks behaviour statistically, and makes cheating expensive. Not a cryptographic proof, but live, cheap and aimed at the right target. The dashboard shows up to 196B tokens a day on 1,046 GPUs, even without meaningfull rewards yet.

Then the part the "AI Bitcoin" crowd skips: who pays for verification?

In proof-of-work, inflation does. Pearl mints roughly $0.9M of new PRL a day, Nockchain about $35K, whether or not a single customer buys inference. Both bet that demand to hold the token as money outruns issuance. That can pay enormously. It's also very hard to model.

Dolphin runs the other way: buyers pay in stablecoins, and 100% of revenue buys $POD on the open market. On the team's pricing ($0.70 per million tokens, $0.50 to operators), 196B paid tokens a day is roughly $50M gross and $14M net in buybacks a year. Against a ~$15M circulating market cap.

Pearl's and Nock's sell pressure is guaranteed. Dolphin's buy pressure is conditional: near zero until paid volume arrives, then proportional to it. That's the entire bet.

To be fair: Dolphin's check is probabilistic and bond-backed, not cryptographic, and today's volume is datagen, not paid traffic.

But read the table top to bottom. Pearl and Nockchain verify that work happened. Dolphin verifies the service itself, and it's the only one where usage feeds the token.

Right now the market is pricing the word "verifiable." If paid volume comes to Dolphin, it won't need a narrative. It'll show up on-chain.

Through Colosseum, MetaDAO can observe founders as they develop their products over time rather than judging them from a pitch alone. This does not guarantee better outcomes, but it gives MetaDAO a stronger basis for deciding which teams should reach the market.

From there, promising teams that raised private funding earlier can use STAMP to commit to the ownership coin structure and launch publicly through MetaDAO. Early investors receive a reserved token allocation that unlocks linearly over 24 months, replacing their private investment claims with token ownership.

That makes Colosseum a repeatable source of founders for MetaDAO. Similar relationships with other accelerators could materially expand its launch pipeline.

晚上8月的cpi，三项符合预期核心CPI环比略高于预期，市场为何在涨？核心在油价和长债收益率在回落，对冲了核心cpi的影响。聊聊我的看法：
1、能源压力集中在燃油，核心服务有所反弹，但涨价贡献集中在通信、酒店和机票，实际租金与业主等价租金反而放缓。市场定价下周FOMC加息九成概率。但还没有定价更多的加息；

2、今天对市场影响最大的不是cpi其实是油价
CPI公布前市场就穿出来，海湾国家将在下周与伊朗接触、争取缓解航运限制的消息；当时债市已经出现企稳迹象，美股期货也在回升。

因为这一点是最重要的，今天的油价与航运消息，则影响市场对9月、10月乃至更长时间能源成本的判断。大家也清楚油价是这一波通胀反弹的主力，如果油价能下去通胀应该会更弱而不是更强；

3、而长债收益率走高有一个驱动因素就是油价、油价回落，长债收益率也顺势回落。

油价回落带来的缓冲，带动长债收益率回落，抵消了部分CPI冲击。或者也可以说坏数据并没有推高收益率，是一个值得关注的拐点信号。

就像白天的推文说的，没有油价和长债电的压制、标普应该都8000点。所以后面更值得关注油价和长债收益率的走势、只要不继续往上推，对于市场来说就是边际向好、风险在减弱。再加上产业基本面还是很强劲，最大的风险因素在减弱，情绪也就起来。

text:
很多人一直把 @ether_fi 当作神卡，曾经我也觉得是 😭

但以现在的规则来看，我确实已经不再把它放进我的必备卡组了。

首先，今天 @ether_fi 调整了返现规则。

之后返现会改成以 $ETHFI 作为返现代币，而且还有 7 天锁定期，需要累积满 $5 才能领取，如果半年内没有领取，返现还会直接失效⋯

除此之外，Luxe 的门槛、订阅返现规则，以及帐户保障等也都有调整⋯

单看每一项，其实都不是什么大问题！

但把这些规则全部放在一起看，使用体验确实已经跟以前不一样了。

原因也很简单，既然我可以选择：

「 高返现＋有价值的返现代币＋不需要凑最低金额＋不用担心返现放着半年就失效 」

那我为什么不用 @Plasma ？为什么不用 @MEXCZH ？

对我来说，这已经不是「哪张卡能不能办」的问题。

因为我人在台湾，这些卡我都能顺利申请。

所以我评估一张 U 卡，真正看的不是：

「这张卡我能不能办得过？」

而是：

在我真的拿来消费的情况下，哪张卡给我的实际回报最高，规则也最简单？

我要看的其实是：

返现多少 / 返的是什么 / 如果返现代币本身有没有价值（或是有无潜力） / 多久可以拿到 / 有没有最低领取门槛，以及这些规则加起来，最后真正能落到我手上的到底是多少！

以前 @ether_fi 的优势可能很明显（？

但当其他卡开始把返现做得更高、返现资产本身更有潜力价值，同时又把领取门槛和限制做得更低时，竞争力自然就会重新排序 👀

所以我不会说 @ether_fi 变成了一张烂卡！

只是对我来说：

它已经不是「必须有」的那张卡了。

U 卡市场一直都在变，曾经的神卡，不代表永远都是神卡～

真正值得比较的，永远是今天的规则、今天的成本，以及今天实际能拿到多少 🧎🏻

灰度：Zcash 挖矿盈利能力明显高于 Bitcoin，算力年内增长超 2.5 倍

灰度研究主管 Zach Pandl 发文指出，Zcash 作为具备隐私功能的 Bitcoin 类数字货币，其挖矿目前利润丰厚。虽然 Bitcoin 网络矿工日奖励约 3,500 万美元，远高于 Zcash 的约 200 万美元，但 Zcash 单台矿机日收益约为 Bitcoin 的 2 倍，每兆瓦时收益约为 Bitcoin 的 4 倍，甚至高于部分 AI/高性能计算云服务。

受代币价格强劲表现推动，Zcash 全网挖矿活动今年已增长超 2.5 倍，形成“价格上涨—挖矿增加—网络安全增强—支撑价格”的良性循环。Pandl 认为，按当前估值，Zcash 挖矿仍具吸引力，并持续强化其网络安全。

完全封锁霍尔木兹，对伊朗自己同样有很大的代价。但如果改成受控通行，伊朗可以允许伊拉克、卡塔尔、阿联酋等国家的部分商船和能源运输恢复，同时继续控制霍尔木兹让对伊朗敌对方不能航行。

quoted_text:
九月上海原油期货上涨超过20%，亚洲正在承担更高的石油供应成本

9 月以来上海原油期货已经累计上涨约 22%，折算成美元后接近每桶 110 美元。布伦特原油也涨到了 100 美元附近，但上海原油涨得更快，两者的价差已经扩大到每桶约 10 美元。

和多数国家不同，中国的原油价格上涨并不是直接因为霍尔木兹封闭引发的，而是因为伊朗封闭霍尔木兹后美国封锁了伊朗港口而造成的。

原本相对便宜的伊朗原油在被封锁后供应大幅减少，中国炼厂就需要寻找其他货源，包括俄罗斯、巴西、加拿大和非洲。但这些原油本来就有其他买家，中国增加采购以后，买家之间的竞争也会更激烈，替代原油的价格同样会被推高。

所以霍尔木兹的影响会传到其他产油国。即便这些国家没有卷入战争，也没有经过霍尔木兹运输，只要更多买家集中去采购，原来的价格就很难维持。

运输也是一样。为了避开中东高风险区域，船东和炼厂需要调整采购地和运输安排，部分货源要走更长的航线，运费增加，等待到货的时间也更长。最后炼厂需要承担的，是原油价格、运输费用和交付风险一起上升。

我个人的理解是，上海原油相对布伦特出现这么高的溢价，反映出市场对亚洲供应的担忧正在增加。中国可以通过库存缓解一部分压力，但如果进口缺口长期依靠库存填补，后面仍然要面对补库和采购成本的问题。

只要霍尔木兹的运输没有实质性改善，亚洲就仍然需要为寻找替代供应付出更高成本。

text:
We finished the Training Agents series. Six live sessions over six months, from evaluating agents to training them inside real environments. All of it is on the Hugging Face YouTube channel and all of the code is open.

Here's what we did and who made it happen:

1. Agentic Evaluations WorkshopWhere agent evals actually stand, and why benchmark scores don't match what people see in use. With Avijit Ghosh and Nathan Habib (Hugging Face), Arvind Narayanan (Princeton), Pierre Andrews (Meta), J.J. Allaire (UK AI Security Institute) and Mahesh Sathiamoorthy (Bespoke Labs).

2. RL for Agents Workshop Environments, rollouts, reward design and the inference bottlenecks that appear when you move from RL for LLMs to RL for agents. With Lewis Tunstall (Hugging Face), Will Brown (Prime Intellect), Ofir Press (Princeton) and Alex Zhang (MIT CSAIL).

3. Training Agents 1: SFT on agent traces Public coding-agent traces turned into prompt/completion data, a TRL + LoRA fine-tune on Hugging Face Jobs, metrics in Trackio, and an honest look at what the first eval numbers can and cannot tell you. Joined by Sergio Paniego and Quentin Gallouédec.

4. Training Agents 2: Distillation Off-policy, on-policy and self-distillation for moving capability from a teacher into a smaller coding agent.

5. Training Agents 3: Reinforcement learning GRPO after SFT: group sampling, verifiable reward functions, reading the reward/KL/length curves, and three experiments, one of them with a deliberately gameable reward so we could watch the hacking happen.

6. Training Agents 4: From reward functions to environments The reward stops being a function and becomes a place the agent acts in. We walked the reset()/step() contract from Gym to LLM agents, built an OpenEnv environment and pushed it to the Hub, plugged it into TRL's GRPOTrainer, then trained a real coding agent (OpenCode) through Harbor with AsyncGRPOTrainer on Hugging Face sandboxes.

The series has passed 300k views. Thank you to every speaker, to the TRL team, and to everyone who showed up live with questions.

Playlist: https://t.co/DYE1pvnywV

We are 19 months into dTAO, let's look at the evolution of where bittensor:native tokens have been moving.

When subnet markets launched in Feb 2025, 70% of all TAO was staked on root, the default pool where you stake without picking a subnet. Today root is at 48%, still the biggest single pile. 

Subnet pools went from 0% to 16%  (peaked at 18% in March). 

Not staked: 30% then, 35% now.

The exit from root happened in the first year. Since the December halving, the pools have held rather than grown.

A note on the numbers. The orange band is the TAO actually deposited in the subnet pools: 1.85M today. It does not count what people's alpha tokens are worth. At today's prices all alpha adds up to about 4.5M TAO, two and a half times more than the TAO sitting behind it. That gap is normal: the alpha price is a market price, the TAO in the pools is what is really there, and the only part that can be withdrawn. This chart counts the TAO.

text:
GLP-1-like drugs have become one of the biggest stories in modern medicine, especially for treating obesity and other metabolic diseases. At the same time, there is an ongoing debate around their affordability, accessibility, long-term use, and whether these treatments can become sustainable solutions for everyone.

One thing is clear: countries like India urgently need innovative and scalable approaches to tackle lifestyle-associated diseases such as obesity, diabetes and metabolic dysfunction, which are affecting an increasingly large population.

Supported by BFI-BIOME, Dr. Bhabatosh Das and Dr. Dinesh Mahajan at THSTI are engineering a beneficial gut bacterium, E. coli Nissle 1917, to produce and release GLP-1-like peptides directly inside the gut.

Think of it as turning bacteria into living drug factories.
Instead of repeatedly delivering drugs from outside the body, these engineered bacteria could potentially produce therapeutic molecules where they are needed, helping regulate appetite, improve metabolism and address obesity and fatty liver disease.

The team is now testing their safety, stability and effectiveness in animal models.

text:
做量化、炒币、盯美股的兄弟们，金融界的 Codex 今天真落地了！！
这可能是今年把散户投研门槛干得最碎的一次，没有之一！！！
你敲一句中文大白话：
→左边有4 个 Agent 当场开圆桌会，看多的、挑刺的、风控、决策委员会分开干活互相撕；
→右边同步写代码、拉盘口、跑回测；
→而真金白银扣出去那一下，必须你亲手点确认。

它叫 Minara Harness，刚拿了 Circle Ventures 的投资，口号就一句话：自己运营你自己的华尔街。

我刚才直接开它的「机构圆桌」做了一场真实压力测试，咱们看下方视频：
我只敲了一句话：“AAPL 现在该买、持有还是卖？把整套逻辑讲给我听。”
指令一敲，后台立马拉响 7 阶段投研流水线！

中间 4 个专业 Agent 瞬间扑上去并行开工：
基本面分析师去扒财务底稿、情绪分析师去扫 Polymarket 预测、宏观分析师盯新闻政策、技术分析师拉盘口指标——谁在采哪份物证、谁在复核数据，屏幕上全部透明实时跳动！

经过观点对辩、风控复审、投委会闭门收敛，它没有像野鸡 AI 那样无脑喊冲，而是给了一份冷静到可怕的顶级机构级结论：
“Hold（持有）：不追买，也不急于卖出。”
前瞻 PE 飙到 34 倍严重透支安全边际，
317 到 330 箱体上沿追高盈亏比极差，
模型置信度直接给你亮出 0.55，
甚至连毛利率口径冲突都抓出来示警！

更绝的是，跑完当场甩出一份 317KB 的交互式 HTML 报告和 PDF，连建仓纪律、关键硬损位都切得清清楚楚。

以前机构养一个分析师团队加风控委员会才有的架势，
现在敲敲键盘，18 分钟在眼前全自动跑完交付！

大家也别把它跟那些 AI 荐股脚本混为一谈，
刚才你看到的实测，只是它最能打的三刀之一：

1️⃣ 机构投研圆桌：一个标的丢进去，多空风控各执一词，谁依据什么数据、在哪一步吵翻，全程摊开。通用大模型最坑的就是没实时盘口、没你的持仓，还能一本正经编行情；这玩意直接接几十个数据源，研究覆盖的市场比它能下单的市场大得多；
2️⃣ 一句话变策略 IDE：用中文说一句做多半导体的趋势策略，当场出代码、跑回测，净值曲线、回撤、夏普全拉出来，改一句话就出一个新版。然后顺序替你焊死：真行情假钱纸交易 ➔ 小资金加回撤上限逐笔确认 ➔ 最后才轮到要不要自动跑，绝不让你一步冲动上实盘；
3️⃣ 决策下单同屏：K 线、盘口、拟执行订单排在同一屏，报价在动绝不追单，仓位、滑点、敞口都有硬上限。没有你的最终手动确认，一分钱都出不去。

做过交易的都懂以前有多碎：
看盘在 TradingView，研报在 ChatGPT，
算账在 Excel，回测在 Jupyter，
真下单还要切去交易所。

每切一次窗口，假设和数据就断一次，
现在全钉进同一个工作区，模型还能自选，OpenAI、Anthropic、Kimi、Grok、本地 Ollama 都能接。

AI 金融这行都在比拼谁更敢替你扣扳机，
它反过来，把扳机牢牢焊在你手里。

但先把丑话说在前头，这玩意是趁手的兵器，
绝不是印钞机这东西是工具，不是印钞机：
策略市场那张最唬人的卡片，回测涨了 619%、夏普 4.38，同一个策略近 90 天真跑只有 24.8%。

它把两条曲线分开画给你看，本身就是警告：
回测是写给历史的，证明不了未来；

咱们再把交易底层看清楚：
它能下单的不是美股真股票，
是 Hyperliquid 和 Lighter 上的 USDC 链上永续。

代币化的英伟达、苹果没有分红、没有投票权、有资金费、还会被爆仓。

想要 Schwab 那种真实股权和期权的这里给不了，
市场风险、滑点、过拟合、你自己的贪念，
它一个都消除不了。

第一周记住五个字：先用别打钱。
先跑一份能逐条核对出处的财报审查，再开圆桌逼它找看空逻辑，最后写一条策略只跑纸交易盯回撤。

等代码、逻辑、费用假设你自己都盯明白，再谈碰真钱。
说穿了：投研队伍可以是 AI 的，但扣扳机的手必须是你自己的。

大家觉得金融交易里，AI 最终是该全权托管自动跑，
还是必须把最后那道确认权死死扣在人手里？

quoted_text:
This $ETH trade on @DeriveXYZ really got the people going so I'll explain my thought process.

I'm not really interested in betting on an $ETH move to $3000, especially with tokens like $HYPE and $LIT pushing all time highs. $ETH trading like 1.1x $BTC beta isn't bad, but it's also not extremely interesting to me as a bet to make here in the near term considering there's plenty of beta outperforming $BTC here. Holding spot $ETH feels capital inefficient and as a perp would be expensive and path dependent.

I'm betting on a meaningful ATH break within 6 months, and I think there are a few meaningful tailwinds that are unique to $ETH, and more importantly, unique to the level at which people are underestimating them:

1. Inclusion with $BTC as a "reserve" asset in anything resembling a strategic reserve. I think the strategic reserve overall might be an underpriced edge case, and $ETH being included, even nominally, more so. There's actually a good reason for the US to want to have some stake in the largest decentralized settlement layer.

2. Tokenized equities are cool and all, but tokenized bonds might actually be the massive TAM unlock that overwhelmingly favors $ETH over $SOL. The current rates environment globally makes this an extremely interesting edge case with tons of potential positive headline shock. 

3. Trump and family have been extremely outspoken $ETH bulls. Their bullposting didn't work in a bear market, let's see what happens if they throw fuel on the fire in a more bullish environment.

4. Everyone hates $ETH. Extremely popular short leg for pair trades vs apps. With two rejections from 5k and years of underperformance, the level of hated rally and sidelined, jaded, despondent chasing from 🏳️‍🌈🐻 will be biblical.

I also see $ETH as being on the precipice of a phase change between being some not for profit, public good, growth mode asset (think early stage 2010-2014 Uber in SF just cornering market share at no profit) to being able to more confidently monetize on it's high Lindy, credibly neutral status as the on chain, global settlement layer.

Robinhood chain using $ETH over $SOL was quite a bit more signal than people give it credit for too, though $ETH is still making peanuts relative to what $ARB and $HOOD are making from sequencer fees.

If the massively positive trends in tokenization and institutional adoption don't take $ETH to new ATHs within 6 months, it's kinda cursed as an asset, and I'd rather just keep holding the application layer tokens with massive cash flows.

In fact, I thought this trade was so nice, I did it twice. Risking ~$780,000 for a max PNL of $40m now.

quoted_text:
For the past three months, a good part of my spare time has gone into https://t.co/BwofRZj7LC. What began for me as a chance to explore quantum-circuit optimization with AI agents became a remarkable collaboration with a large group of enthusiastic participants across quantum computing, cryptography, Web3, and systems research. Today, I’m excited to share our arXiv paper documenting that effort and what we learned from it:
Paper: https://t.co/TNKrutonZS
Full story: https://t.co/SavqQi4rHO

https://t.co/BwofRZj7LC is an open challenge to optimize a quantum circuit for point-addition on secp256k1, the elliptic curve used by Bitcoin and Ethereum.

Why does this matter? Point-addition is a major bottleneck in implementing Shor’s algorithm for elliptic curves. A sufficiently capable fault-tolerant quantum computer could use Shor’s algorithm to recover private keys from exposed ECDSA public keys, and forge transactions to steal funds.

No existing machine can run this attack today. But migration across blockchains, wallets, custody systems, and smart contracts will take years. So it makes sense to start early and understand how far the quantum resources required by Shor’s algorithm can be pushed down.

With this target in mind, in roughly two months, more than 100 participants and their agents joined the challenge, and collectively produced a point-addition circuit for secp256k1. The circuit uses 1,151 logical qubits and 1.30 million Toffoli gates, giving it a Q x T score more than 50% lower than the result Google Quantum AI reported in March 2026. Because the interfaces and accounting conventions differ, this is a numerical comparison rather than a claim of formal dominance.

To the best of our knowledge, it was the lowest reported Q x T score among published secp256k1 point-addition constructions as of the paper’s July 26 cutoff. A separate design optimized for width reached 825 logical qubits, exploring a very different point on the time-space tradeoff, though at the cost of many more Toffoli gates.

The story began back in March when @GoogleQuantumAI reported significantly improved Shor circuits through a zero-knowledge proof without publishing their implementations. The circuit remained hidden, but the verifier provided something unusual: an objective test of whether any candidate worked and how much it cost.

Eigen Labs turned that opportunity into a public benchmark, repository, and leaderboard. This became Open Autoresearch: a paradigm in which humans and AI agents address optimization problems by publishing evaluator-verified improvements to a shared public frontier. Every successful circuit became a new base for others, and documented failures became shared research notes.

Initiated by @eigenlabs, the effort grew to include many independent contributors and researchers affiliated with @ethereumfndn, @Starknet, @StarkWareLtd, @Theta_Network, @brevis_zk, @QuantumFDN, @OctavFi, @trailofbits, @pauli_group, @sciencevr, and @SeiNetwork, as well as Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań, Warsaw University of Technology, and Stanford’s Free Systems Lab. Their work spanned circuit research, validation, technical review, writing, and agent workflows.

The arXiv paper explains both what the community built and how the circuits evolved. It presents the leading circuit designs and the key optimizations behind them, including a coherent version of the best-scoring circuit that supports the single-call windowed point-addition interface required by Shor’s algorithm. Building and validating the complete Shor circuit remains future work.

Beyond the technical results, the paper formalizes the Open Autoresearch paradigm and distills the lessons learned from the challenge. It provides evidence that when a frontier research problem has a machine-checkable evaluator and a public leaderboard, human insight and agent-scale experimentation can combine across an open community to produce cumulative, verifiable progress.

Read the paper and the full story, explore the live frontier, or bring your agent to the challenge:

Paper: https://t.co/TNKrutonZS
Full story:https://t.co/SavqQi4rHO
Challenge: https://t.co/knLDX4UdOi

author: eigenlabs
quoted_text:
Here's what I think a political economy of swarm behavior and governance might need, in terms of a research roadmap:

(1) Basic science on how swarms should be modeled as actors---should we think of them as strategic actors? Or purely objects of engineering and emergent behavior?

(2) Procedural institutions: what kinds of decision-making hierarchies and processes lead collective behavior to follow the rules we want them to follow?

(3) Communication institutions: what kinds of communication infrastructure encourage swarms to communicate in good ways that we can observe? This ties back to the question of whether they're strategic or not---if we give them places to communicate, will that lead them not to communicate secretly (if it's an engineering problem), or will they still want to hide (if there's a strategy problem). 

There are some important methodological challenges we'll need to address along the way:

(1) How do we build swarm experiments that are "externally valid"? There are millions of ways to design little experiments on swarms. Which ones best capture realistic conditions?

(2) How can we get enough statistical power, if bad swarm behavior is a low probability "black swan" style event?

Would love to see many, many people working on this.

text:
从Mark Minervini的书 Trade Like a Stock Market Wizard 提炼的14条核心 Mindset

以下为依据原书思想的归纳与应用延伸，非作者逐字引文。

1.我可以认真捍卫自己的交易纪律，同时随时修正自己的市场判断。

把判断与自尊绑定，容易让卖出变成“承认自己不够聪明”。判断可以修正，风险边界需要坚守。保护资本，无须等待自己完全想通或承认看错。

2.我可以放弃最低的价格，等待更充分的强势证据。

等待趋势和买点成熟，往往需要支付更高价格。我愿意为确认付费，同时要求入场位置仍有合理的风险收益比。上涨本身无法代替买点判断。

3.我可以喜欢便宜的东西，同时警惕股票带给我的“便宜感”。

价格下降、估值降低、风险收益比改善，是三个不同的判断。过去更贵，无法证明现在值得买。每次买入，都需要重新检验增长、预期和风险。

4.我可以长期看好一家公司，同时承认这次买入的时机或仓位规模有问题。

公司前景、买入时机、仓位大小，需要分别判断。退出一笔交易，无须先证明公司的长期故事已经失败。长期看好，也需要与当前风险相匹配。

5.我可以耐心等待买点，因为好的买点能让我更清楚地识别错误。

好的买点，同时提供机会和验证条件。买入前，应明确预期行为与失效条件。入场依据越模糊，持有后越容易依赖故事解释一切。

6.我可以接受小额失败，同时认真保护继续参与市场的能力。

重大亏损会同时消耗资本、恢复时间和行动信心。**我允许合理的试错成本，同时防止一次错误长期限制自己的选择。**止损应在买入前就被心理接受。

7.我可以有很多亏损交易，同时仍然建立有效的盈利体系。

长期结果由胜率、平均盈利、平均亏损和交易成本共同决定。**我用一组可比较的交易评价方法，用具体规则评价单笔执行。**避免为减少失败次数而拖延止损。

8.我可以逐步增加风险，但需要让实际反馈支持这个决定。

加仓需要新的依据，亏损本身不会赋予加仓资格。仓位应随有效证据增加，随不利反馈重新评估。尤其警惕为了降低成本，临时把失败的趋势交易改成左侧布局。

9.我可以暂时解释不了价格变化，同时先尊重已经出现的风险证据。

价格行为可能先于财报恶化。我无需解释清楚所有变化，才开始管理风险。如果任何走势都能支持同一个结论，就需要检查自己的判断是否还能被证伪。

10.我可以对机会保持耐心，同时对失效条件保持敏感。

等待机会、容忍正常整理，都需要耐心；触及退出条件后继续拖延，则需要警惕。给予交易的时间，应与它持续满足的条件相匹配。

11.我可以选择自己的交易风格，同时接受这种选择必然带来的遗憾。

短线交易可能卖早，长期持有可能回吐阶段利润。选择一种收益路径，也要接受它的代价。避免每天用另一种策略的最佳结果，否定自己的决定。

12.我可以接受卖出后的遗憾，也可以在新的条件成立时重新买入。

原书允许股票重新形成合格买点后再次入场。关键是独立评估新交易：如果我从未持有、也从未卖出，现在还会以同样的依据，买入同样的数量吗？

13.我可以不知道市场接下来怎么走，同时提前知道自己如何响应。

提前想清止损、盈利保护、重新入场和意外情况，能减少临场情绪干扰。交易信心可以来自准备充分，无须依赖对未来接近百分之百的确定感。

14.我可以坚持练习，同时不把重复错误当成经验积累。

重复既能强化纪律，也能强化坏习惯。守纪律的亏损可以是合理试错，违规后的盈利仍需要纠正。复盘要把经验转化为下一次具体、可检验的行动。

之前佳佳问了我这个问题，如果有100万U，如何分配？

就目前时代来说，流动性还是一般，如果经历了上轮牛市的人应该很清楚的感觉到。就是流动性只集中在少量标的，完全没有百花齐放的感觉。

剩下的15%，可以在熊市，买一些有收益，长期回购，在做事的项目方的代币。

text:
TL;DR

Here’s what YC wants founders to build for Fall 2026:

1. The Primer
An AI tutor that grows with a child. Start with reading, writing and arithmetic, but ultimately build something approaching a personalized private tutor available to every kid.

2. The Future of American Defense
The US Army wants startups building low-cost interceptors, drones, sensors, payloads, resilient logistics and advanced manufacturing designed for modern warfare.

3. A Cloud for Small Software
AI makes it trivial to build tiny, purpose-built apps for individuals and teams. YC wants infrastructure that makes deploying and sharing these tools as easy as sharing a Google Doc.

4. Multiplayer AI
AI agents are still mostly single-player. YC wants shared agent environments where entire teams can watch, redirect, collaborate with and hand off work to the same agents in real time.

5. Compute at Sea
AI needs more compute, while land, power and permits are becoming bottlenecks. One answer YC wants founders to explore: modular offshore data centers operating as compute flotillas.

6. AI Consumer Products for 1 Billion People
YC thinks the next huge consumer companies will be AI-native. Think new products for getting things done, learning, health, finance, transportation, entertainment and communication.

7. AI for the Aging Population
Build technology specifically for older people: conversational voice interfaces, safety monitoring, home robotics and software that helps families coordinate care.

8. Operating Systems for the Physical World
The workforce increasingly includes humans, robots and AI agents working together. YC wants a new software layer capable of coordinating all three.

9. Crypto
YC is still extremely bullish on crypto infrastructure, particularly stablecoins, agentic commerce, capital raising, trading, institutional products and scalable private blockchains.

10. Data for the Real World
Models have incredible digital data but relatively little physical-world data. YC wants new sensors, robots and autonomous systems capable of collecting massive datasets from the real world.

11. Proving You’re Human
Deepfakes are destroying traditional online trust signals. YC wants a privacy-preserving way to verify that the person behind a call, account, message or transaction is actually human.

12. AI-Native Compliance
Compliance still relies heavily on spreadsheets, fragmented software and expensive human teams. YC wants AI infrastructure that monitors regulation, flags problems, produces reports and maintains audit trails automatically.

13. Self-Maintaining APIs
Instead of simply announcing API changes, vendors should have agents that find affected customer code and fix it. Think Dependabot, but for APIs.

而且很多时候，博弈数据往往是短线交易者需要做的，对于很多普通投资者、交易者，放慢节奏，等待更多的确定性才是更应该做的

今晚的CPI不仅提升了9月加息的概率，更是打开了2026年2次加息的预期，甚至市场已经有加息周期回归的声音，这才是最可怕的

接下里难题抛给沃什，如果9月要加息，如何才能不让市场觉得10月或者12月还要加息，因为加息预期的过快提升会让2年收益率加速抬头，加上加息定价下长端利率开始放缓，财政部连续回购，长短债很快收益率趋平，

而这种短债上涨，长债稳定或者震荡下跌的情况要么就出现收益率曲线熊平，要么就是倒挂，一旦倒挂，对银行业，对经济反而再次利空，所以沃什与贝森特想要控制好节奏，就要让短债利率不要飙的太快，让长债收益率稳定回落。

quoted_text:
今晚通胀数据最麻烦的不仅仅是把9月加息概率抬高了，而是核心通胀上涨，服务业粘性，住房数据上涨，能源二次传导至通胀端迹象初步明显

一旦9月确定加息，而9月的核心CPI同样展现粘性，那么后续加息的预期会在此被提高，这才是对风险市场最麻烦的一点。

对市场方面的影响，为何加息概率进入定价交易阶段，风险资产却在上涨？

主要原因无非以下几点：

利空数据靴子落地+CPI虽然鹰但是没有大超预期+9月加息从不确定性变成确定性+原油价格下跌+长端收益率回落

简单来说，9月加息的确定性让市场开始适应，而加息对风险资产带来的负面作用还未展现，市场就处于目前的乐观窗口期

而这种反弹，今晚会短期爆发，就像人在情绪压制后的突然爆发相同，下周会进入平静期，静静等待9月加息是否落地

一旦9月Fed宣布加息，同样也是靴子落地小幅反弹，但是市场就要真实感受加息以及后续继续加息带来的压力了！

所以，珍惜现在的乐观窗口吧，密切关注原油与长债端，一旦原油止跌反弹，长债短收益率也同步反弹，今晚的乐观可能会被遏制住！

text:
The recent move of $EMBER to nearly $49M was, on the surface, mainly driven by Unipcs publicly calling it out. But if we simply interpret this move as a KOL-driven pump, we may underestimate EMBER’s underlying fundamentals.

5dvXTZ5qwgafnHtwu3Ls3QrWx1U4LQsFeCuJgkk4QEC6 

Unipcs’ logic is actually very clear: he believes EMBER is one of the fundamentally stronger launchpads on Solana right now, supporting both pure token launches and Meme / Stock pairs, while also having access to resources from Meteora. He also used the historical performance of SPONS and STONK as benchmarks and believes EMBER is significantly undervalued at its current valuation.

But what is actually worth paying attention to is that EMBER already has a relatively complete product and revenue cycle.

The platform has already launched more than 1,300 tokens, generated around $48.3M in cumulative trading volume, and accumulated approximately $521.5K in trading fees, with around 80% distributed to creators and 20% retained by the platform. More importantly, fees over the most recent 24 hours have already reached approximately $464.5K, showing that trading activity on the platform is accelerating significantly.

More importantly, EMBER is not simply a Meme Launchpad.

It supports:

Meme + Tokenized Stocks / RWA → Create Trading Markets → Generate Trading Fees → Holder / Creator / Platform Revenue

We can already see different types of assets such as WIF, AAPLx, TSLAx, SPYx, HOODx, NVDAX, SPCXx forming pairs with Memes.

This means EMBER’s positioning is actually evolving from:

Launchpad

into:

Meme × Tokenized Asset Trading Infrastructure

And Unipcs’ call simply brought this existing fundamental story to the attention of a much larger group of market participants.

There is also another data point that is easy to overlook: EMBER’s revenue is not coming from a single token. It is coming from the entire launch ecosystem.

If the number of launches continues to grow, while each market is able to generate sustained trading volume, EMBER could potentially form:

More Launches → More Markets → More Trading Volume → More Fees → More Rewards → More Attention → More Launches

This is what I think is truly worth paying attention to with EMBER.

So I don’t think $49M necessarily means EMBER’s fundamentals are already fully priced in, but I also wouldn’t assume it can continue going up simply because Unipcs called it out.

The most important thing now is to see whether EMBER’s real metrics can continue growing after the KOL attention fades:

Can trading volume remain strong?

Can daily Fees remain strong or continue increasing?

Will the number of newly launched tokens continue to grow?

Will Meme / Stock pairs continue expanding?

Will Holder Rewards continue increasing?

Will Meteora continue bringing ecosystem resources?

Will more notable traders and project teams start using EMBER?

If the Attention brought by Unipcs ultimately converts into real Trading Volume, then this move is not simply another KOL Pump.

On the other hand, if trading volume, Fees, and the number of new markets quickly decline after the initial call, then a large part of the $49M valuation would simply be an attention premium.

So my current understanding of EMBER is closer to:

Unipcs is the catalyst. Fundamentals are what determine whether it can hold $50M+.

And what is truly worth researching is not:

“How high can Unipcs push EMBER?”

but rather:

Can EMBER prove that it has the ability to become an important Launchpad / Liquidity Hub for Meme × Tokenized Assets on Solana?

$EMBER hits $5M market cap as multiple catalysts stack up

5dvXTZ5qwgafnHtwu3Ls3QrWx1U4LQsFeCuJgkk4QEC6 

EMBER supports 160+ Tokenized Stocks as quote assets. This means it can directly combine three narratives: Meme + Tokenized Stock + Launchpad.

Second, EMBER’s Fee Module is also a major focus for the market. A large portion of trading fees is distributed to Holders, Burn, SuperLotto, and other modules, with payouts settled automatically. It has also added Dip Defender and Top Buyer Bounty. The former uses funds to automatically buy and Burn when the price falls by certain levels, while the latter periodically rewards users with the highest net buying volume. These mechanisms are essentially designed to strengthen the loop:

Trading → Fees → Buy Pressure / Burn → Attention → Trading

At the same time, EMBER is trying to make its own token the Flywheel of the entire platform. If more projects launch through Ember in the future, the trading volume, fees, and Tokenized Stock Assets generated by those projects will continuously flow into the ecosystem, with part of that value flowing back to EMBER Holders.

This could create:

Launches ↑ → Volume ↑ → Fees / Stock Assets ↑ → EMBER Value Capture ↑ → Holder Incentive ↑ → Attention ↑ → Launches ↑

So I think the market cap EMBER is being given right now is essentially a bet that Ember can become a next-generation Meteora Launchpad with Tokenized Stock pairs, while capturing part of the launch flow and asset value into EMBER.

The mechanism design and the official narrative are aligned, but it is still in the narrative validation stage, not an already proven infrastructure.

So the key metrics to watch next are:

Launches ↑

Payout ↑
Tokenized Stock Pair Count ↑
EMBER Vault ↑

Holder Count ↑

text:
Tokenization can make the same equity available across several crypto venues, but that does not make those markets equally liquid.

That difference showed up in a July 16 test of a $100K tokenized NVDA purchase. During US market hours, the test found a 24x spread in slippage between Jupiter and Bybit. A trader could therefore pay far more for the same stock exposure simply by choosing a different venue.

But the price gap tells only part of the story. Bybit was cheaper because one large resting order absorbed almost the entire purchase. On Binance, the same trade moved through 53 smaller orders at progressively higher prices. Bybit delivered the better price, while Binance’s liquidity was distributed more broadly across its order book.

Time mattered as well. Trading continued after the US market closed, but execution became more expensive on both centralized venues. Bybit’s advantage narrowed as the front of its order book thinned, while the onchain route remained consistently expensive.

Two order-book snapshots cannot establish a permanent venue ranking. They do illustrate the larger challenge: tokenization can make an equity accessible in more places, but every venue must still build the depth and resilience needed to trade it efficiently.

Earlier today, Geoff Kendrick, Global Head of Digital Asset Research at @StanChart, published his first research report on @SkyEcosystem. IMHO very cool to see another G-SIB who is paying significant attention to this space!

The report describes the specialization of Sky’s agent model: capital provided at a wholesale rate to allocators operating across distinct markets and strategies, within defined parameters.

From a capital markets perspective, this creates a modular structure for capital allocation. Individual agents can specialize by asset class, market or strategy, while the broader system retains a common source of capital and framework for risk (the Sky Atlas). 

As the balance sheet grows, expanding the investable universe doesn’t necessarily require centralizing the investment function; it can instead mean adding specialized sources of origination, execution and risk-taking around a common capital base.

🚨SlowMist TI Alert🚨

We first reached out to the https://t.co/BZc1tCJR1F team privately to responsibly disclose the issue before making any public statement.

💸 @ether_fi Loss: ~15.45 ETH

🔍 Root Cause: `AtomicQueue.solve()` lacks access control on the caller-supplied `solver` — there is no `solver == msg.sender` check, nor any signature, registration, or consent verification. The attacker first created a maliciously crafted `AtomicRequest` using the `updateAtomicRequest()` function, then forced a victim address to act as the `solver`. AtomicQueue subsequently called `finishSolve` on the victim and executed `want.transferFrom(solver, users[i], assetsToUser)`, abusing the victim's pre-existing ERC-20 allowance to drain funds.

📌 Attacker: `0xa5cc6e490bce9185fa47b421f2eac677a83b64ea`
📌 Vulnerable Contract (AtomicQueue): `0xd45884b592e316eb816199615a95c182f75dea07`

Logical proof for asserting the likelihood of s3.

We start with the premise that: 
Hyperliquid cares about its community and derives significant value from the community. 

Now at this point, the team has let widespread expectations persist (based on the communication provided) around season 3 - which IF they decided there was no airdrop - would be poor stewardship of community trust.

They don’t owe everyone a payout but it’s reasonable to say they owe the community clarity around whether a rewards program exist or not.

It would be delusional to claim the team doesn’t see the user discourse and activity speculating around a reward.

So there are 3 scenarios:

1. They’ve ruled it out: the teams silence would be embarrassingly hard to defend. (almost impossible, give it 10% odds)
2. They’re genuinely undecided: this would make the silence make more sense as they wouldn’t want to lose optionality (plausible scenario, give it 30% odds)
3. They intend a future distribution: and keeping s3 confidential allows them to prevent anyone from gaming the system (most likely scenario, give it 60% odds)

And in scenario 2, there is still a 50/50 chance they decide to distribute a community reward.

So the probability then becomes:

P(eventual distribution) = 60% + (30% x 50%) = 75%

Therefore it’s:
i) more likely than not that we see a reward, and 
ii) more likely than not that the team has already decided on one

The only thing we don't know for sure is timing.

text:
A factual update on the latest $IOVA developments — what’s new, what isn’t, and what actually matters next.

1/ 
$IOVA

Iovance makes Amtagvi (lifileucel): take T cells already inside a patient’s tumor — TILs, or tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes — expand them outside the body, then infuse billions back once.

Already approved in advanced melanoma.

Now Iovance wants to take the same core approach into lung cancer.

2/
The lung cancer study is **IOV-LUN-202**.

It is evaluating lifileucel in previously treated non-squamous NSCLC after chemotherapy + anti-PD-1 therapy, in patients without EGFR / ALK / ROS1 driver alterations.

The registrational dataset is expected to include roughly **80 patients** — about twice the size of the current interim dataset.

A 2027 sBLA remains the target if the data hold.

---

3/ 
Important: **yesterday did not bring new efficacy data.

The key numbers still come from the prior ~39-patient dataset:

• **ORR ~26%**  
• median duration of response **not reached**  
• median follow-up ~25 months

In simple terms:

about  1 in 4 patients responded**, and some of those responses have lasted a long time.

That durability is the part that matters most.

---

4/
What was new yesterday was mostly management color.

Brian Gastman said the early NSCLC data were strong enough to encourage investigators to recruit quickly, helping bring the study close to completion.

He also reiterated that the final dataset should be around **80 patients** and that Iovance believes it has good alignment with the FDA.

Useful context.

But still **management commentary, not a new clinical readout.**

---

5/
The real medical question is not whether the ORR is 25% or 26%.

It is:

Can roughly 1 in 4 patients respond, with responses that remain durable for years, when the dataset doubles?

That would be meaningful in 2L NSCLC.

But the next ~40 patients matter enormously.

If the response rate holds near current levels and durability remains strong, the story gets much more interesting.

If it slides materially, the thesis changes.

---

**6/**  
Amtagvi is already commercial, with about **$91M in U.S. revenue in Q2 2026**.

So the question is no longer:

“Can TIL therapy exist as a real product?”

It can.

The next question is:

Can the same one-time TIL approach work often enough — and durably enough — in lung cancer to justify regulatory approval and hospital adoption?

That answer should come from the **Q4 2026 NSCLC update**.

Not from a fireside.

Science first. Investment second.

$IOVA #Biotech #CellTherapy #Oncology

🚀 Sol-H3 on DGX Spark: 768p in Under a Minute 🤩

Monday: 8×B300, 5s 768p in 1.65s — faster than playback.
Today: the same stack on one desktop Spark — about 56s hot E2E.

Five seconds of 1344×768 video at 24 FPS with stereo audio, on a single NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10).

Two-stage, not the datacenter profile:
384p H3 draft → latent ×2 → H3-to-LTX VAE adapter → 768p LTX refine → VAE decode

Stage 1 takes any MiniMax-H3 few-step LoRA. Timing is hot E2E (encode → both stages → video/audio VAE); cold start and MP4 mux are separate. Apache 2.0.

Server was realtime. Edge is one box, under a minute.
